translations.idiomatic: Ling Yunyi

sentences.zh: 譚綸，字子理，宜黃人。

translations.literal: Tan Lun, styled Zili, was a native of Yihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Lun, courtesy name Zili, came from Yihuang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign (1544).

sentences.zh: 除南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 歷職方郎中，遷臺州知府。

translations.literal: He served successively as a director in the Ministry of War and was transferred to prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Ministry of War to director, then was transferred to serve as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 綸沈毅知兵。

translations.literal: Lun was deep and resolute and understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was grave, resolute, and versed in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時東南倭患已四年，朝議練鄉兵禦賊。

translations.literal: At that time the pirate calamity in the southeast had already lasted four years, and the court debated training militia to resist the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Wokou had ravaged the southeast for four years, and court opinion favored training local militia to resist them.

sentences.zh: 參將戚繼光請期三年而後用之。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Qi Jiguang requested a three-year period before putting them to use.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Qi Jiguang asked for three years before his troops would be ready for action.

sentences.zh: 綸亦練千人。

translations.literal: Lun also trained a force of one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Lun likewise drilled a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 立束伍法，自裨將以下節節相制。

translations.literal: He established a squad-binding law whereby from assistant commanders downward each level controlled the next.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted a chain-of-command system in which every officer down to the assistant commanders was bound to control the rank below.

sentences.zh: 分數既明，進止齊一，未久即成精銳。

translations.literal: Once the subdivisions were clear, advance and halt were uniform; before long they became crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: With ranks clearly defined, movement and halts were perfectly coordinated, and in short order they became an elite force.

sentences.zh: 倭犯柵浦，綸自將擊之，三戰三捷。

translations.literal: When the pirates attacked Zhapu, Lun led the troops himself to strike them and won three battles in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates struck Zhapu, Lun took the field in person and won three victories in a row.

sentences.zh: 倭復由松門、澶湖掠旁六縣，進圍臺州，不克而去。

translations.literal: The pirates again came by Songmen and Chanhu, plundering six neighboring counties, then advanced to besiege Taizhou but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders returned via Songmen and Chanhu, looted six neighboring counties, and marched on Taizhou; failing to take the city, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 轉寇仙居、臨海，綸擒斬殆盡。

translations.literal: They then turned to raid Xianju and Linhai; Lun captured and beheaded nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Xianju and Linhai, they were hunted down until Lun had captured and beheaded nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 進海道副使，益募浙東良家子教之，而繼光練兵已及期，綸因收之以為用，客兵罷不復調。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the maritime circuit and recruited more sons of good families in eastern Zhejiang to train them; by then Jiguang's troops had completed their term of training, and Lun took them into his service, while hired troops from elsewhere were dismissed and no longer levied.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice commissioner for the coastal circuit, he recruited more local youths from eastern Zhejiang for training. Qi's men had by then finished their three-year drill, and Lun incorporated them into his command while disbanding the hired auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 倭自象山突臺州，綸連破之馬崗、何家覽，又與繼光共破之葛埠、南灣。

translations.literal: Pirates bursting out from Xiangshan rushed on Taizhou; Lun repeatedly defeated them at Magang and He Jialan, and together with Jiguang he again broke them at Gebu and Nanwan.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates erupted from Xiangshan against Taizhou, Lun routed them at Magang and He Jialan, then with Qi Jiguang crushed them again at Gebu and Nanwan.

sentences.zh: 加右參政，會憂去。

translations.literal: He was given the additional rank of right assistant administrator, but when a bereavement occurred he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant administrator, then left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 以尚書楊博薦起，復將浙兵，討饒平賊林朝曦。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Minister Yang Bo he was recalled to service and again led Zhejiang troops to suppress the Raoping bandit Lin Chaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Minister Yang Bo, he returned to command Zhejiang forces against the Raoping rebel Lin Chaoxi.

sentences.zh: 朝曦者，大盜張璉余黨也。

translations.literal: Chaoxi was a remnant follower of the great pirate Zhang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxi had been a lieutenant of the great pirate Zhang Lian.

sentences.zh: 璉既滅，朝曦據巢不下，出攻程鄉。

translations.literal: After Lian was destroyed, Chaoxi held his lair and would not submit, then came out to attack Chengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Lian's destruction, Chaoxi held out in his stronghold, then sallied forth to attack Chengxiang.

sentences.zh: 知縣余甫宰嚴兵待，而遣主簿梁維棟入賊中，諭散其黨。

translations.literal: Magistrate Xu Puzai made strict military preparations while sending registrar Liang Weidong into the bandit camp to persuade their followers to disperse.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xu Puzai mustered a stern defense while sending registrar Liang Weidong into the rebel camp to persuade the rank and file to scatter.

sentences.zh: 朝曦窮，棄巢走，綸及廣東兵追擒之。

translations.literal: Chaoxi, driven to extremity, abandoned his lair and fled; Lun and the Guangdong troops pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Chaoxi abandoned his nest and fled; Lun and the Guangdong troops ran him down and captured him.

sentences.zh: 尋改官福建，乞終制去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his post was changed to Fujian, but he begged leave to complete his mourning and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Fujian but petitioned to finish his mourning leave and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 繼光數破賊，浙東略定。

translations.literal: Jiguang repeatedly defeated the bandits, and eastern Zhejiang was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang's repeated victories largely pacified eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 倭轉入福建。

translations.literal: The pirates then shifted into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates then shifted their operations into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 自福寧至漳、泉，千里盡賊窟，繼光漸擊定之。

translations.literal: From Funing to Zhang and Quan, a thousand li were all bandit dens; Jiguang gradually attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: From Funing to Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, pirate nests stretched a thousand li; Qi Jiguang gradually fought them down.

sentences.zh: 師甫旋，其眾復犯邵武，陷興化。

translations.literal: Hardly had the army withdrawn when their bands again raided Shaowu and took Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Scarcely had the army withdrawn when the raiders struck Shaowu and captured Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 四十二年春，再起綸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the forty-second year he was again summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the forty-second year (1563), Lun was summoned back to service.

sentences.zh: 道擢右僉都御史，巡撫福建。

translations.literal: En route he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: While still on the road he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 倭屯崎頭城，都指揮歐陽深搏戰中伏死，倭遂據平海衛，陷政和、壽寧，各扼海道為歸計。

translations.literal: Pirates were encamped at Qitou Fort; the regional commander Ouyang Shen fought fiercely, fell into an ambush, and died, whereupon the pirates seized Pinghai Guard, took Zhenghe and Shouning, and each held the sea lanes as their route of escape.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates held Qitou Fort. Regional commander Ouyang Shen fought fiercely, was ambushed and killed, and the enemy then seized Pinghai Guard and overran Zhenghe and Shouning, each detachment blocking the sea lanes for retreat.

sentences.zh: 綸環柵斷路，賊不得去，移營渚林。

translations.literal: Lun ringed them with palisades and cut their roads so they could not leave, and the bandits moved camp to Zhulin.
translations.idiomatic: Lun encircled them with stockades and severed their escape routes; the bandits then shifted camp to Zhulin.

sentences.zh: 繼光至，綸自將中軍，總兵官劉顯、俞大猷將左、右軍。

translations.literal: When Jiguang arrived, Lun personally led the center army while regional commanders Liu Xian and Yu Dayou led the left and right armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Jiguang arrived, Lun commanded the center in person while Liu Xian and Yu Dayou led the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 令繼光以中軍薄賊壘，左右軍繼之，大破賊，復一府二縣。

translations.literal: He ordered Jiguang with the center army to press the bandit stockade while the left and right armies followed up, inflicting a great defeat and recovering one prefecture and two counties.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Qi to press the rebel camp with the center while the wings followed up. The enemy was shattered and one prefecture and two counties were recovered.

sentences.zh: 詔加右副都御史。

translations.literal: An edict added to him the rank of right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 綸以延、建、汀、邵間殘破甚，請緩征蠲賦。

translations.literal: Lun, seeing how badly Yan, Jian, Ting, and Shao had been ravaged, requested deferred levies and remission of taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the devastation across Yan, Jian, Ting, and Shao, Lun petitioned for tax relief and remission of levies.

sentences.zh: 又考舊制，建水砦五，扼海口，薦繼光為總兵官以鎮守之。

translations.literal: He also examined the old regulations, built five river forts to choke the estuaries, and recommended Jiguang as regional commander to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: He revived the old system of five river forts to guard the estuaries and recommended Qi Jiguang as regional commander to hold them.

sentences.zh: 倭復圍仙遊，綸、繼光大破賊城下。

translations.literal: The pirates again besieged Xianyou; Lun and Jiguang inflicted a great defeat on them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates again besieged Xianyou, Lun and Qi Jiguang routed them beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 已而繼光破賊王倉坪、蔡丕嶺，余賊走，廣東境內悉定。

translations.literal: Before long Jiguang defeated the bandits at Wangcangping and Caipiling; the remaining bandits fled, and within Guangdong all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qi broke the enemy at Wangcangping and Caipiling; the remnants fled, and Guangdong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 綸上疏請復行服，世宗許之。

translations.literal: Lun memorialized asking to resume mourning garb, and the Jiajing Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lun petitioned to return to mourning dress, and the Jiajing Emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 四十四年冬，起故官，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-fourth year he was recalled to his former post as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the forty-fourth year (1565) he was recalled to his former post as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上而大足民作亂，陷七城。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, the people of Dazu rose in revolt and seized seven cities.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the people of Dazu rebelled and captured seven cities.

sentences.zh: 詔改綸四川，至已破滅。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Lun to Sichuan, but by the time he arrived the rebels had already been destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reassigned him to Sichuan; by the time he arrived the uprising had already been crushed.

sentences.zh: 雲南叛酋鳳繼祖遁入會理，綸會師討平之。

translations.literal: The Yunnan rebel chieftain Feng Jizu had fled into Huili; Lun joined forces and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan rebel Feng Jizu had fled into Huili; Lun combined forces and brought him to submission.

sentences.zh: 進兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督兩廣軍務兼巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: He was advanced to right vice minister of war with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, and made supreme commander of the military affairs of the two Guang and grand coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice minister of War with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, serving as supreme commander of the two Guang and grand coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 招降嶺崗賊江月照等。

translations.literal: He received the surrender of the Linggang bandits Jiang Yuezhao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the surrender of Linggang bandits such as Jiang Yuezhao.

sentences.zh: 綸練兵事，朝廷倚以辦賊，遇警輒調，居官無淹歲。

translations.literal: Lun was skilled in military affairs, and the court relied on him to handle bandits; whenever an alarm arose he was transferred, and he never held any post for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in military affairs, he was the man the court turned to whenever banditry flared; he was constantly reassigned and rarely held any post for even a year.

sentences.zh: 迨南寇略平，而邊患方未已。

translations.literal: By the time southern banditry was largely settled, border troubles had still not ended.
translations.idiomatic: Southern piracy was largely subdued, but border crises were only beginning.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，給事中吳時來請召綸、繼光練兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, the supervising secretary Wu Shilai requested that Lun and Jiguang be summoned to train troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing (1567), supervising secretary Wu Shilai petitioned to recall Lun and Qi Jiguang to drill troops.

sentences.zh: 詔征綸還部，進左侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Lun back to the ministry and promoted him to left vice minister with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, as supreme commander of the Ji, Liao, and Baoding military circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was recalled to the ministry, promoted to left vice minister with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, and made supreme commander of Ji, Liao, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 綸上疏曰：

translations.literal: Lun memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lun submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 薊、昌卒不滿十萬，而老弱居半，分屬諸將，散二千里間。

translations.literal: The garrison troops of Ji and Chang number fewer than one hundred thousand, of whom half are old and weak, assigned to various generals and scattered over two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji and Chang garrisons field fewer than one hundred thousand men, half of them aged or unfit, parcelled out among various commanders across two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 敵聚攻，我分守，眾寡強弱不侔，故言者亟請練兵。

translations.literal: When the enemy masses to attack, we divide to defend; in numbers, strength, and weakness we are unequal—hence critics urgently call for training troops.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy concentrates for attack while we divide to defend; in numbers and fighting strength we are mismatched. That is why everyone urges troop training.

sentences.zh: 然四難不去，兵終不可練。

translations.literal: Yet until four difficulties are removed, troops in the end cannot be trained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet four obstacles must be cleared before training can succeed.

sentences.zh: 夫敵之長技在騎，非召募三萬人勤習車戰，不足以制敵。

translations.literal: The enemy's special strength lies in cavalry; unless thirty thousand men are recruited and drilled assiduously in chariot warfare, they cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy excels at cavalry. Unless thirty thousand men are levied and drilled in chariot tactics, we cannot counter them.

sentences.zh: 計三萬人月餉，歲五十四萬，此一難也。

translations.literal: Calculating monthly rations for thirty thousand men, the annual cost is five hundred forty thousand taels—this is the first difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand men cost five hundred forty thousand taels a year in pay alone—the first difficulty.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙之士銳氣盡於防邊，非募吳、越習戰卒萬二千人雜教之，事必無成。

translations.literal: The fighting spirit of Yan and Zhao men has been exhausted on border defense; unless twelve thousand battle-seasoned troops from Wu and Yue are recruited and mixed in for instruction, the affair will certainly fail.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Zhao warriors have spent their edge on routine border duty. Unless twelve thousand veterans from Wu and Yue are recruited and trained alongside them, the plan cannot work.

sentences.zh: 臣與繼光召之可立至，議者以為不可。

translations.literal: Your servant and Jiguang can summon them and they will arrive at once, yet critics say this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang and I can summon such men immediately, yet critics object.

sentences.zh: 信任之不專，此二難也。

translations.literal: Trust in us is not exclusive—this is the second difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: We are not given sole authority—this is the second difficulty.

sentences.zh: 軍事尚嚴，而燕、趙士素驕，驟見軍法，必大震駭。

translations.literal: Military affairs demand severity, yet men of Yan and Zhao are by nature arrogant; confronted suddenly with military law they will be greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: War demands harsh discipline, yet Yan and Zhao soldiers are proud by nature. Sudden exposure to strict military law will shock them.

sentences.zh: 且去京師近，流言易生，徒令忠智之士掣肘廢功，更釀他患，此三難也。

translations.literal: Moreover, being near the capital, rumors spread easily; loyal and capable men will only have their hands tied and their achievements ruined, breeding further troubles—this is the third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is near, so rumors fly easily. Able and loyal officers will be hamstrung and their work undone, inviting fresh disasters—the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 我兵素未當敵，戰而勝之，彼不心服。

translations.literal: Our troops have never matched the enemy in battle; if we fight and win, they will not submit in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Our men have seldom bested the enemy. A single victory will not win their respect.

sentences.zh: 能再破，乃終身創，而忌嫉易生；

translations.literal: Only after a second defeat will they bear the wound for life, and jealousy is easily aroused;
translations.idiomatic: A second crushing blow is needed to break their spirit for good—and that is when envy and obstruction arise.

sentences.zh: 欲再舉，禍已先至。

translations.literal: if one wishes to strike again, calamity has already arrived beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: By the time we wish to strike again, disaster has already struck us first.

sentences.zh: 此四難也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth difficulty.

sentences.zh: 以今之計，請調薊鎮、真定、大名、井陘及督撫標兵三萬，分為三營，令總兵參遊分將之，而授繼光以總理練兵之職。

translations.literal: As for the present plan, I request transferring thirty thousand men from the Ji garrison, Zhending, Daming, Jingxing, and the commanders' and coordinators' personal battalions, dividing them into three camps under regional commanders, garrison commanders, and mobile commanders, and entrusting Jiguang with overall charge of training.
translations.idiomatic: My proposal: transfer thirty thousand men from the Ji garrison, Zhending, Daming, Jingxing, and the various commanders' and coordinators' personal battalions; organize them into three camps under regional, garrison, and mobile commanders; and give Qi Jiguang overall charge of training.

sentences.zh: 春秋兩防，三營兵各移近邊。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn the two border-defense seasons, each of the three camps shall move its troops nearer the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn defense season, all three camps shall shift closer to the border.

sentences.zh: 至則遏之邊外，入則決死邊內。

translations.literal: When the enemy comes, hold them beyond the border; if they enter, fight to the death within the border.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy approaches, block them beyond the wall; if they break in, fight to the death inside it.

sentences.zh: 二者不效，臣無所逃罪。

translations.literal: If neither course succeeds, your servant has no escape from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If both strategies fail, I accept full punishment.

sentences.zh: 又練兵非旦夕可期，今秋防已近，請速調浙兵三千，以濟緩急。

translations.literal: Moreover, training troops cannot be expected overnight; the autumn defense is already near—please quickly transfer three thousand Zhejiang troops to meet the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Training cannot be accomplished overnight, and autumn defense is upon us. Please urgently transfer three thousand Zhejiang troops to cover the gap.

sentences.zh: 三年後，邊軍既練，遣還。

translations.literal: After three years, when the border troops are trained, send them back.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, when the border forces are trained, they may be sent home.

sentences.zh: 詔悉如所請，仍令綸、繼光議分立三營事宜。

translations.literal: An edict approved everything requested and still ordered Lun and Jiguang to deliberate the details of establishing the three separate camps.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every request and ordered Lun and Qi Jiguang to work out the details of the three-camp system.

sentences.zh: 綸因言：「薊鎮練兵逾十年，然竟不效者，任之未專，而行之未實也。

translations.literal: Lun then said: "Troop training in the Ji garrison has gone on for more than ten years, yet in the end it has had no effect because responsibility was not exclusive and execution was not real.
translations.idiomatic: Lun added: "The Ji garrison has drilled troops for over ten years without result because no one had sole responsibility and nothing was carried through.

sentences.zh: 今宜責臣綸、繼光，令得專斷，勿使巡按、巡關御史參與其間。」

translations.literal: Now Lun and Jiguang should be charged and granted sole decision-making power, and touring censors and pass inspectors must not interfere.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jiguang and I should be given full authority to decide matters, without interference from touring or pass inspectors.

sentences.zh: 自兵事起，邊臣牽制議論，不能有為，故綸疏言之。

translations.literal: From the time military affairs began, border officials had been constrained by debate and could accomplish nothing—hence Lun's memorial spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Since the border wars began, frontier officers had been tied down by wrangling and could achieve little—hence Lun's blunt memorial.

sentences.zh: 而巡撫劉應節果異議，巡按御史劉、巡關御史孫代又劾綸自專。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Coordinator Liu Yingjie in fact raised objections, and the touring censor Liu and pass inspector Sun Dai also impeached Lun for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Yingjie dissented, while touring censor Liu and pass inspector Sun Dai impeached Lun for arrogating authority.

sentences.zh: 穆宗用張居正言，悉以兵事委綸，而諭應節等無撓。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor, following Zhang Juzheng's advice, entrusted all military affairs to Lun and instructed Yingjie and the others not to obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong, heeding Zhang Juzheng, placed all military affairs in Lun's hands and told Liu Yingjie and the rest not to interfere.

sentences.zh: 綸相度邊隘沖緩，道里遠近，分薊鎮為十二路，路置一小將，總立三營：東駐建昌備燕河以東，中駐三屯備馬蘭、松、太，西駐石匣備曹墻、古石。

translations.literal: Lun surveyed the border passes for points of thrust, slackness, distance, and proximity, divided the Ji garrison into twelve routes with a junior commander on each route, and established three camps in all: the eastern camp at Jianchang to guard east of the Yan River, the central at Santun for Malan, Song, and Tai, and the western at Shixia for Caojiang and Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: Lun surveyed every pass for vulnerability and distance, divided the Ji garrison into twelve sectors each under a junior commander, and set up three camps: the east at Jianchang covering the country east of the Yan River; the center at Santun for Malan, Song, and Tai; the west at Shixia for Caojiang and Gushi.

sentences.zh: 諸將以時訓練，互為掎角，節制詳明。

translations.literal: The generals trained on schedule, mutually supporting like pincers, with regulations clear in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders drilled on schedule, mutual support arranged like pincers, regulations spelled out in detail.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，薊、昌無警。

translations.literal: That autumn Ji and Chang were free of alarms.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Ji and Chang saw no alarms.

sentences.zh: 異時調陜西、河間、正定兵防秋，至是悉罷。

translations.literal: In former times troops from Shaanxi, Hejian, and Zhengding were levied for autumn defense; from this time onward all such levies ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Shaanxi, Hejian, and Zhengding troops were drafted each autumn; now those drafts ended.

sentences.zh: 綸初至，按行塞上，謂將佐曰：「秣馬厲兵，角勝負呼吸者，宜於南；

translations.literal: When Lun first arrived he inspected the frontier and told his officers: "Feeding horses, sharpening weapons, and deciding victory in the breath of a moment suit the south;
translations.idiomatic: On first arriving he toured the defenses and told his officers: "Feeding horses, sharpening blades, and winning in an instant—that is the southern way.

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，坐制侵軼者，宜於北。」

translations.literal: fortifying walls, clearing the countryside, and sitting to control raids suit the north.
translations.idiomatic: Strong walls, cleared fields, and passive control of raids—that is the northern way.

sentences.zh: 遂與繼光圖上方略，築敵臺三千，起居庸至山海，控守要害。

translations.literal: He then joined Jiguang in drawing up frontier plans and built three thousand watch towers from Juyong to Shanhai to guard the critical points.
translations.idiomatic: He and Qi Jiguang then drafted frontier strategy and built three thousand watchtowers from Juyong to Shanhai to hold the vital points.

sentences.zh: 綸召入為右都御史兼兵部左侍郎，協理戎政。

translations.literal: Lun was summoned in as right censor-in-chief with concurrent appointment as left vice minister of war, assisting in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as right censor-in-chief and left vice minister of War, assisting in military administration.

sentences.zh: 會臺工成，益募浙兵九千余守之。

translations.literal: When the tower works were completed, he recruited more than nine thousand Zhejiang troops to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tower works were finished, he recruited over nine thousand more Zhejiang troops to man them.

sentences.zh: 邊備大飭，敵不敢入犯。

translations.literal: Border defenses were greatly tightened, and the enemy did not dare to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Border defenses were greatly strengthened, and the enemy no longer dared raid.

sentences.zh: 以功進兵部尚書兼右都御史，協理如故。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was advanced to minister of war with the concurrent rank of right censor-in-chief, his assisting duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was promoted to minister of War with the concurrent rank of right censor-in-chief, retaining his assisting duties.

sentences.zh: 其冬，予告歸。

translations.literal: That winter he was granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was granted leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，起兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor took the throne, he was appointed minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Lun was appointed minister of War.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，加太子少保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Wanli reign he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 給事中雒遵劾綸不稱職。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Luo Zun impeached Lun as unfit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Luo Zun impeached him as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 綸三疏乞罷，優詔留之。

translations.literal: Lun three times memorialized begging to be dismissed, but gracious edicts kept him in post.
translations.idiomatic: Lun thrice petitioned to resign, but gracious edicts kept him at his post.

sentences.zh: 五年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli (1577) he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangmin (Assiduous and Keen).

sentences.zh: 綸終始兵事垂三十年，積首功二萬一千五百。

translations.literal: Lun was involved in military affairs from beginning to end for nearly thirty years and accumulated a head-count merit of twenty-one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly thirty years Lun was continuously engaged in military affairs, amassing a credited head count of twenty-one thousand five hundred.

sentences.zh: 嘗戰酣，刃血漬腕，累沃乃脫。

translations.literal: Once in the heat of battle, blood from his blade soaked his wrist; it took repeated dousing before he could remove his armor.
translations.idiomatic: Once, blood from his blade soaked his wrist in the heat of battle; it took repeated rinsing before he could take off his armor.

sentences.zh: 與繼光共事齊名，稱「譚、戚」。

translations.literal: Serving together with Jiguang, he was equally famed—they were called "Tan and Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Serving alongside Qi Jiguang, he shared equal fame; together they were known as "Tan and Qi."

sentences.zh: 徐甫宰，字允平，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Xu Puzai, styled Yunping, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Puzai, courtesy name Yunping, was from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中舉順天鄉試，除武平知縣。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing era he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed magistrate of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 武平當閩、粵交，多盜，甫宰築城立堡者三。

translations.literal: Wuping lay where Fujian and Guangdong met and had many bandits; Puzai built a city wall and established three forts.
translations.idiomatic: Wuping lay on the Fujian–Guangdong border and was rife with bandits; Puzai walled the city and built three forts.

sentences.zh: 上官以程鄉賊盜藪，調之往。

translations.literal: His superiors, because Chengxiang was a bandit lair, transferred him there.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chengxiang was a bandit stronghold, his superiors transferred him there.

sentences.zh: 既平朝曦，超擢潮州兵備僉事，添註剿寇，任一子千戶。

translations.literal: After Chaoxi was pacified he was specially promoted to Fujian vice commissioner for military preparedness in Chaozhou, with an additional commission to suppress bandits, and one son was granted the rank of chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin Chaoxi's defeat he was specially promoted to Chaozhou vice commissioner for military preparedness with an added mandate to suppress bandits; one son was granted the rank of chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 已而程鄉賊溫鑒、梁輝等合上杭賊窺江西。

translations.literal: Before long the Chengxiang bandits Wen Jian and Liang Hui and others joined with Shanghang bandits to spy on Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chengxiang bandits Wen Jian, Liang Hui, and others allied with Shanghang rebels to probe into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 平遠知縣王化遮擊之檀嶺，賊敗奔瑞金，副使李佑三戰皆捷。

translations.literal: The Pingyuan magistrate Wang Hua intercepted them at Tanling; the bandits were defeated and fled to Ruijin, and Vice Commissioner Li You won three battles in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan magistrate Wang Hua blocked them at Tanling. Defeated, they fled toward Ruijin, where Vice Commissioner Li You won three victories in a row.

sentences.zh: 賊由間道歸程鄉，甫宰討擒之，余黨悉平。

translations.literal: The bandits returned by a bypath to Chengxiang; Puzai attacked and captured them, and the remaining followers were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels doubled back to Chengxiang by a hidden route; Puzai pursued, captured them, and pacified the rest.

sentences.zh: 賚銀幣。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 已，補潮州分巡僉事兼理兵備事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Chaozhou vice commissioner for circuit inspection with concurrent charge of military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Chaozhou circuit intendant with concurrent charge of military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 東莞水兵徐永太等亂，停俸討賊。

translations.literal: The Dongguan naval troops under Xu Yongtai and others mutinied; his salary was suspended while he campaigned against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongguan naval troops under Xu Yongtai mutinied, his salary was suspended while he campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 甫宰已疾亟，乞歸。

translations.literal: Puzai was already gravely ill and begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Already gravely ill, Puzai petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 王化，字汝贊，廣西馬平人。

translations.literal: Wang Hua, styled Ruzan, was a native of Maping in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, courtesy name Ruzan, was from Maping in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父尚學，職方郎中。

translations.literal: His father Shangxue had been a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Shangxue had served as a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 化登鄉薦。

translations.literal: Hua passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十年，新置平遠縣，授化知縣。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Jiajing the newly established Pingyuan County had Hua appointed its magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of Jiajing (1561), when Pingyuan County was newly created, Wang Hua was appointed its magistrate.

sentences.zh: 以擊賊檀嶺，有知兵名。

translations.literal: For striking bandits at Tanling he gained a reputation for understanding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His victory at Tanling won him a reputation as a man who understood war.

sentences.zh: 田坑賊梁國相既降復叛，約三圖賊葛鼎榮等分寇江西、福建。

translations.literal: The Tiankeng bandit Liang Guoxiang had surrendered but rebelled again, joining with the Santu bandit Ge Dingrong and others to raid Jiangxi and Fujian in concert.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiankeng bandit Liang Guoxiang, having surrendered, rebelled again and joined Ge Dingrong of Santu and others to raid Jiangxi and Fujian in concert.

sentences.zh: 化寄妻子會昌，而身率鄉兵往擊。

translations.literal: Hua sent his wife and children to Huichang while he personally led militia to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua sent his family to Huichang and led the militia in person.

sentences.zh: 賊連敗，乃縱反間會昌，言化已歿，化妻計氏慟哭自刎。

translations.literal: After repeated defeats the bandits spread disinformation in Huichang that Hua had died; Hua's wife, the Lady Ji, wailed and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: After successive defeats the rebels spread word in Huichang that Wang Hua was dead. His wife Lady Ji wept and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 化怒，追賊益急，獲國相於石子嶺。

translations.literal: Enraged, Hua pursued the bandits all the more urgently and captured Guoxiang at Shiziling.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Wang Hua pressed the pursuit and captured Guoxiang at Shiziling.

sentences.zh: 遷潮州府同知，仍署縣事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Chaozhou while still acting as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant prefect of Chaozhou while continuing to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 計被旌，官為立祠。

translations.literal: The Lady Ji was given an official commendation and a shrine was erected for her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ji was officially commended and a shrine was erected in her honor.

sentences.zh: 化舉卓異，超擢廣東副使。

translations.literal: Hua was nominated as outstanding and was specially promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in personnel review, he was specially promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 南贛巡撫吳百朋以貪黷劾之，削籍。

translations.literal: The Nanzhen grand coordinator Wu Baipeng impeached him for corruption and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhen grand coordinator Wu Baipeng impeached him for corruption and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史趙淳薦其知兵，乃命以僉事飭惠、潮兵備。

translations.literal: Touring censor Zhao Chun recommended his knowledge of military affairs, and he was ordered to serve as vice commissioner overseeing military preparedness in Huizhou and Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Zhao Chun praised his military knowledge, and he was reappointed vice commissioner for Huizhou and Chaozhou military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 久之，考察罷。

translations.literal: After a long time he was dismissed in the regular personnel review.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was dismissed in the regular personnel review.

sentences.zh: 李佑，字吉甫，貴州清平衛人。

translations.literal: Li You, styled Jifu, was a native of the Qingping Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li You, courtesy name Jifu, was from the Qingping Guard in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing (1547).

sentences.zh: 歷官江西副使，邀賊瑞金有功。

translations.literal: He served successively as Jiangxi vice commissioner and had merit in intercepting bandits at Ruijin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangxi vice commissioner and distinguished himself intercepting bandits at Ruijin.

sentences.zh: 尋敗廣東賊吳誌高、江西下歷賊賴清規等，皆賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he defeated the Guangdong bandit Wu Zhigao and the Jiangxi Xialü bandit Lai Qinggui and others, and in each case was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the Guangdong bandit Wu Zhigao and the Jiangxi Xialü rebel Lai Qinggui, earning silver and silk rewards each time.

sentences.zh: 進江西右參政。

translations.literal: He was advanced to right assistant administrator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right assistant administrator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵官俞大猷，大破劇賊李亞元。

translations.literal: Together with the regional commander Yu Dayou he inflicted a great defeat on the major bandit Li Yayuan.
translations.idiomatic: With regional commander Yu Dayou he inflicted a crushing defeat on the major bandit Li Yayuan.

sentences.zh: 擢僉都御史，巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 屢敗海寇林道乾、山寇張韶南等。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the sea bandit Lin Daogan and the mountain bandit Zhang Shaonan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated the sea pirate Lin Daogan and the mountain bandit Zhang Shaonan.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，被劾罷歸。

translations.literal: In the Longqing era he was impeached and dismissed, returning home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing era he was impeached, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 王崇古，字學甫，蒲州人。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu, styled Xuefu, was a native of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu, courtesy name Xuefu, came from Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Jiajing (1541).

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 由郎中歷知安慶、汝寧二府。

translations.literal: From director he served successively as prefect of Anqing and Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from director, he served successively as prefect of Anqing and Runing.

sentences.zh: 遷常鎮兵備副使，擊倭夏港，追殲之靖江。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparedness in Changzhen, struck the pirates at Xiagang, and pursued and destroyed them at Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Changzhen military vice commissioner, he attacked pirates at Xiagang and pursued them to destruction at Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 從巡撫曹邦輔戰滸墅。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Coordinator Cao Bangfu in battle at Huxu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Grand Coordinator Cao Bangfu at Huxu.

sentences.zh: 已，偕俞大猷追倭出海。

translations.literal: Later he joined Yu Dayou in driving the pirates out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Yu Dayou in driving pirates out to sea.

sentences.zh: 累進陜西按察使，河南右布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Shaanxi surveillance commissioner and Henan right administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Shaanxi surveillance commissioner to right administration commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，改右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was changed to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year (1564) he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 崇古喜譚兵，具知諸邊厄塞，身歷行陣，修戰守，納降附，數出兵搗巢。

translations.literal: Chonggu delighted in military discussion, knew thoroughly every frontier choke point, personally went through the ranks, repaired defense and offense, accepted surrenders, and several times led troops to raid enemy nests.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu loved military study, knew every frontier pass intimately, took the field in person, strengthened defenses, accepted defectors, and repeatedly led raids on enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 寇屢殘他鎮，寧夏獨完。

translations.literal: Bandits repeatedly ravaged other commands, but Ningxia alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: While raiders devastated neighboring commands, Ningxia alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，加右副都御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was given the additional rank of right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Longqing he received the additional rank of right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 吉囊子吉能據河套為西陲諸部長，別部賓兔駐牧大、小松山，南擾河、湟番族，環四鎮皆寇。

translations.literal: Jineng, son of Tümen, held the Ordos as chief of the western frontier tribes; another branch under Bintu pastured on Great and Little Songshan, raiding south into the He and Huang Tibetan peoples, and bandits surrounded all four commands.
translations.idiomatic: Jineng, son of Tümen, held the Ordos as leader of the western tribes. Another branch under Bintu grazed Great and Little Songshan, raiding south against the Huang and He Tibetan peoples, so that bandits threatened all four commands.

sentences.zh: 總督陳其學無威略，總兵官郭江、黃演等皆敗死，陜西巡撫戴才亦坐免。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue lacked a firm strategy; regional commanders Guo Jiang, Huang Yan, and others were all defeated and killed, and Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Dai Cai was also dismissed for his connection.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Chen Qixue lacked a decisive strategy. Regional commanders Guo Jiang and Huang Yan were defeated and killed, and Shaanxi grand coordinator Dai Cai was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 其冬，進崇古兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督陜西、延、寧、甘肅軍務。

translations.literal: That winter Chonggu was advanced to right vice minister of war with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, as supreme commander of the military affairs of Shaanxi, Yan, Ning, and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chonggu was promoted to right vice minister of War with the concurrent rank of right vice censor-in-chief, supreme commander of Shaanxi, Yan, Ning, and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 崇古奏給四鎮旗牌，撫臣得用軍法督戰，又指畫地圖，分授諸大將趙岢、雷龍等。

translations.literal: Chonggu memorialized granting the four commands command flags so that coordinators could use military law to supervise battle, and also drew maps and distributed them to the major generals Zhao Ke, Lei Long, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for command flags in all four sectors so coordinators could enforce military law in battle, drew maps, and distributed them to major generals such as Zhao Ke and Lei Long.

sentences.zh: 數有功。

translations.literal: He achieved merit on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: He scored repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 著力兔行牧河東，龍潛出興武襲破其營，斬獲多，加崇古右都御史。

translations.literal: Zhulitu grazed east of the river; Long secretly marched out from Xingwu, stormed and broke his camp, and beheaded and captured many; Chonggu was given the additional rank of right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhulitu grazed east of the Yellow River, Lei Long stole out from Xingwu, stormed his camp, and took many heads. Chonggu was promoted to right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 吉能犯邊，為防秋兵所遏，移營白城子。

translations.literal: Jineng raided the border but was blocked by the autumn-defense troops and moved camp to Baichengzi.
translations.idiomatic: Jineng raided the border but was blocked by autumn-defense troops and shifted camp to Baichengzi.

sentences.zh: 龍等出花馬池、長城關與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Long and others came out from Huamachi and Changcheng Pass to give battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Long and others sallied from Huamachi and Changcheng Pass and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 崇古在陜七年，先後獲首功甚多。

translations.literal: Chonggu was in Shaanxi for seven years and in all periods obtained a great many head-count merits.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu spent seven years in Shaanxi and accumulated a large head-count merit record.

sentences.zh: 自河套以東宣府、大同邊外，吉囊弟俺答、昆都力駐牧地也。

translations.literal: East of the Ordos, beyond the borders of Xuanfu and Datong, were the pasturelands where Tümen's younger brothers Altan and Qoton lived.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Ordos, beyond the Xuanfu and Datong borders, lay the pastures of Tümen's younger brothers Altan and Qoton.

sentences.zh: 又東薊、昌以北，吉囊、俺答主土蠻居之，皆強盛。

translations.literal: Further east, north of Ji and Chang, Tümen, Altan, and the ruling Tümen Mongols dwelt—all were powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Farther east, north of Ji and Chang, Tümen, Altan, and the ruling Tümen Mongols held sway—all formidable powers.

sentences.zh: 俺答又納叛人趙全等，據古豐州地，招亡命數萬，屋居佃作，號曰板升。

translations.literal: Altan also harbored the defector Zhao Quan and others, seized the old Fengzhou territory, and recruited tens of thousands of fugitives who built houses, farmed fields, and were called "banshan" settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Altan also sheltered the defector Zhao Quan, seized old Fengzhou territory, and gathered tens of thousands of fugitives who built houses, farmed fields, and formed the so-called banshan settlements.

sentences.zh: 全等尊俺答為帝，為治城郭宮殿；

translations.literal: Quan and the others honored Altan as emperor and built city walls and palaces for him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Quan and his followers hailed Altan as emperor and built walls and palaces for him.

sentences.zh: 亦自治第，制度如王者，署其門曰開化府。

translations.literal: they also built mansions for themselves with institutions like those of kings, and inscribed their gate with the name "Kaifua Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: They built mansions for themselves with regal appointments and inscribed their gate "Kaifua Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 又日夜教俺答為兵。

translations.literal: They also day and night instructed Altan in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night they drilled Altan in the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 東入薊、昌，西掠忻、代，遊騎薄平陽、靈石，至潞安以北。

translations.literal: East they entered Ji and Chang; west they plundered Xin and Dai; roaming cavalry pressed close to Pingyang and Lingshi, reaching north of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: They raided east into Ji and Chang, west into Xin and Dai, and their roaming horsemen pressed as far as Pingyang, Lingshi, and north of Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 起嘉靖辛丑，擾邊者三十年，邊臣坐失事得罪者甚眾，患視陜西四鎮尤劇。

translations.literal: From the xinchou year of Jiajing they had harassed the borders for thirty years; very many border officials were punished for failures, and the affliction in the four Shaanxi commands was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the xinchou year of Jiajing (1541) they had harassed the frontier for thirty years. Countless border officials were punished for failure, and the four Shaanxi commands suffered worst of all.

sentences.zh: 朝廷募獲全者官都指揮使，賞千金，卒不能得。

translations.literal: The court offered the rank of regional commander and a reward of one thousand taels of silver to whoever captured Quan alive, yet in the end he could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The court promised the rank of regional commander and a thousand taels of silver for capturing Zhao Quan alive, yet he was never taken.

sentences.zh: 邊將士率賄寇求和，或反為用；

translations.literal: Border officers and soldiers mostly bribed the bandits to seek peace, or were even turned to the enemy's use;
translations.idiomatic: Border officers and soldiers mostly bribed the raiders for peace, or were even turned into enemy agents.

sentences.zh: 諸陷寇自拔歸者，輒殺之以冒功賞；

translations.literal: those who had escaped from the enemy and returned of their own accord were promptly killed to claim merit rewards;
translations.idiomatic: Defectors who escaped and returned were often killed so officials could claim merit rewards.

sentences.zh: 敵情不可得，而軍中動靜敵輒知。

translations.literal: enemy intelligence could not be obtained, yet the enemy always knew the movements within our camps.
translations.idiomatic: The court could learn nothing of enemy intentions, while the enemy always knew our army's movements.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，詔崇古總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year an edict made Chonggu supreme commander of the military affairs of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year (1570) an edict appointed Chonggu supreme commander of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 崇古禁邊卒闌出，而縱其素通寇者深入為間。

translations.literal: Chonggu forbade border soldiers from straying out while allowing those who had long communicated with the bandits to penetrate deep as spies.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu forbade border troops from straying out while sending long-time contacts with the enemy deep into their territory as spies.

sentences.zh: 又檄勞番、漢陷寇軍民，率眾降及自拔者，悉存撫之。

translations.literal: He also issued proclamations comforting Tibetan, Han, and captive soldiers and civilians who led masses in surrender or escaped on their own, all to be preserved and settled.
translations.idiomatic: He also issued proclamations reassuring Tibetan, Han, and captive troops and civilians who came over in groups or escaped on their own, promising them protection.

sentences.zh: 歸者接踵。

translations.literal: Returnees came in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors streamed in without pause.

sentences.zh: 西番、瓦剌、黃毛諸種一歲中降者逾二千人。

translations.literal: Among the western Tibetans, Oirats, and Yellow Hair tribes, more than two thousand surrendered within one year.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year more than two thousand western Tibetans, Oirats, and Yellow Hair tribesmen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其冬，把漢那吉來降。

translations.literal: That winter Batu Palsin came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Batu Palsin came over to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 把漢那吉者，俺答第三子鐵背臺吉子也。

translations.literal: Batu Palsin was the son of Tiebei Taiji, who was the third son of Altan.
translations.idiomatic: Batu Palsin was the son of Tiebei Taiji, Altan's third son.

sentences.zh: 幼失父，育於俺答妻一克哈屯。

translations.literal: He lost his father in childhood and was raised by Altan's wife, Lady Eke Khatun.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by Altan's wife Lady Eke Khatun.

sentences.zh: 長娶大成比妓不相得。

translations.literal: When he grew up he married Dacheng Bij, but they did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he married Dacheng Bij, but the marriage was unhappy.

sentences.zh: 把漢自聘我兒都司女，號三娘子，即俺答外孫女也。

translations.literal: Batu betrothed himself to a daughter of the Oiradusi, called the Third Lady—she was also Altan's granddaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Batu betrothed himself to a daughter of the Oiradusi, known as the Third Lady—who was also Altan's granddaughter.

sentences.zh: 俺答見其美，奪之。

translations.literal: Altan saw her beauty and seized her.
translations.idiomatic: Altan saw her beauty and took her for himself.

sentences.zh: 把漢恚，又聞崇古方納降，是年十月，率妻子十余人來歸。

translations.literal: Batu was enraged, and hearing that Chonggu was accepting surrenders, in the tenth month of that year he led his wife and more than ten others to come over.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, and hearing that Chonggu was receiving defectors, in the tenth month he led his wife and more than ten followers to the Ming side.

sentences.zh: 巡撫方逢時以告。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Fang Fengshi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Fang Fengshi reported the event.

sentences.zh: 崇古念因此制俺答，則趙全等可除也，留之大同，慰藉甚至。

translations.literal: Chonggu thought that by using this to control Altan, Zhao Quan and the others could be removed; he detained Batu at Datong and comforted him with extreme generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggu saw in this a lever against Altan that could eliminate Zhao Quan and his faction. He kept Batu at Datong and treated him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 偕逢時疏聞於朝曰：「俺答橫行塞外幾五十年，威制諸部，侵擾邊圉。

translations.literal: Together with Fengshi he memorialized the court, saying: "Altan has rampaged outside the passes for nearly fifty years, awing the tribes by his might and harassing our borders.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Fang Fengshi he memorialized the throne: "Altan has rampaged beyond the passes for nearly fifty years, tyrannizing the tribes and harassing our borders.

sentences.zh: 今神厭兇德，骨肉離叛，千里來降，宜給宅舍，授官職，豐餼廩服用，以悅其心，嚴禁出入，以虞其詐。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has turned against his vicious virtue, flesh and bone have split apart, and from a thousand li they have come to surrender—we should grant them residences, confer offices, and provide abundant grain, stipends, and clothing to please their hearts, while strictly forbidding coming and going to guard against deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has turned from his wickedness; his kin have split away and come a thousand li to submit. We should grant them housing and office, supply grain, stipends, and clothing to win their hearts, and strictly control their movements against treachery.

sentences.zh: 若俺答臨邊索取，則因與為市，責令縛送板升諸逆，還被掠人口，然後以禮遣歸，策之上也。

translations.literal: If Altan comes to the border to demand them back, then use that occasion to trade with him, requiring that he bind and send the banshan rebels and return the people he has seized, and only then send Batu back with ceremony—this is the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: If Altan comes to the border to demand him back, negotiate: require him to deliver the banshan rebels bound and return seized subjects, then ceremoniously send Batu home—the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 若遂桀驁稱兵，不可理諭，則明示欲殺，以撓其誌。

translations.literal: If he then acts violently and raises troops beyond reason, then make clear our intent to kill Batu and break his will.
translations.idiomatic: If he grows violent and raises troops beyond negotiation, make plain our willingness to execute Batu and break his resolve.

sentences.zh: 彼望生還，必懼我制其死命。

translations.literal: He will hope for Batu's survival and surely fear that we control his life;
translations.idiomatic: Longing for Batu's survival, he will fear that we hold his life in our hands.

sentences.zh: 誌奪氣沮，不敢大逞，然後徐行吾計，策之中也。

translations.literal: his will shaken and his spirit discouraged, he will not dare act greatly, and then we may slowly carry out our plan—this is the middling stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit broken, he will not dare act boldly; then we may slowly execute our plan—the middling strategy.

sentences.zh: 若遂棄而不求，則當厚加資養，結以恩信。

translations.literal: If we simply abandon him and do not seek anything in return, then we should richly support him and bind him with grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: If we simply abandon him and demand nothing in return, we should richly support him and bind him with grace and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其部眾繼降者，處之塞下，即令把漢統領，略如漢置屬國居烏桓之制。

translations.literal: As for his followers who continued to submit, they should be settled below the passes and placed under Batahan's command, broadly on the model of how the Han stationed dependent states among the Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Those of his followers who kept surrendering should be settled inside the frontier and put under Batahan's leadership—much as the Han once stationed dependent states among the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 他日俺答死，子辛愛必有其眾。

translations.literal: When Altan Khan dies one day, his son Senge will surely hold his following.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan dies, his son Senge will inevitably inherit his following.

sentences.zh: 因加把漢名號，令收集余眾，自為一部。

translations.literal: Batahan should then be given a title and ordered to gather the remainder into a separate tribe of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Grant Batahan a title and charge him to gather the remnants into a tribe of his own.

sentences.zh: 辛愛必忿爭。

translations.literal: Senge will certainly resent this and contend for power.
translations.idiomatic: Senge will surely resent it and fight over the succession.

sentences.zh: 彼兩族相持，則兩利俱存，若互相仇殺，則按兵稱助。

translations.literal: If the two factions hold each other in check, both sides' interests are preserved; if they slaughter one another, we hold our troops and offer aid in name only.
translations.idiomatic: If the two factions balance each other, both our interests are served; if they turn on each other, we keep our armies still and offer only nominal assistance.

sentences.zh: 彼無暇侵陵，我遂得休息，又一策也。

translations.literal: They will have no leisure to raid us, and we may rest—yet another stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: They will lack leisure to raid us, and we shall gain respite—yet another stratagem.

sentences.zh: 若循舊例安置海濱，使俺答日南望，侵擾不已；

translations.literal: If we follow the old practice of settling them on the coast so that Altan Khan looks south day after day, raids will never cease;
translations.idiomatic: If we follow precedent and settle them on the coast, Altan Khan will gaze southward daily and raids will never end;

sentences.zh: 又或給配諸將，使之隨營立功，彼素驕貴不受驅策，駕馭茍乖，必滋怨望，頓生飏去之心，終貽反噬之禍，均為無策。」

translations.literal: or if we assign them to various generals to earn merit in camp, they are by nature proud and high-born and will not accept driving; if command is ill fitted, resentment will grow, the impulse to bolt will arise at once, and in the end we invite the disaster of being turned upon—all equally bad policies."
translations.idiomatic: or if we parcel them out to generals to win merit in the camps—they are proud by nature and will not be driven; mishandle them and resentment will swell, they will flee in a breath, and we shall invite a turning of fangs upon us. All alike are no policy at all."

sentences.zh: 奏至，朝議紛然。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, court debate was tumultuous.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, opinion was sharply divided.

sentences.zh: 御史饒仁侃、武尚賢、葉夢熊皆言敵情叵測。

translations.literal: Censors Rao Renkan, Wu Shangxian, and Ye Mengxiong all said the enemy's intentions could not be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Rao Renkan, Wu Shangxian, and Ye Mengxiong all warned that the enemy's intentions were unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 夢熊至引宋受郭藥師、張瑴事為喻。

translations.literal: Ye Mengxiong even cited the Song's acceptance of Guo Yaoshi and Zhang Jue as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengxiong went so far as to cite the Song's reception of the defectors Guo Yaoshi and Zhang Jue.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書郭乾不能決，大學士高拱、張居正力主崇古議。

translations.literal: Minister of War Guo Qian could not decide; Grand Secretaries Gao Gong and Zhang Juzheng strongly upheld Wang Chonggu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Guo Qian could not decide; Grand Secretaries Gao Gong and Zhang Juzheng forcefully backed Wang Chonggu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 詔授把漢指揮使，賜緋衣一襲，而黜夢熊於外，以息異議。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Batahan battalion commander, granted him one suit of scarlet robes, and transferred Ye Mengxiong elsewhere to quiet dissent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Batahan battalion commander, bestowed a suit of scarlet robes, and posted Ye Mengxiong away from court to still the controversy.

sentences.zh: 俺答方掠西番，聞變急歸，調辛愛兵分道入犯，索把漢甚急。

translations.literal: Altan Khan was raiding the western Tibetans when he heard of the crisis and hurried back; he mobilized Senge's troops to invade by separate routes and demanded Batahan with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan was plundering the western Tibetans when news of the crisis brought him racing home. He sent Senge's forces in by separate routes and urgently demanded Batahan's return.

sentences.zh: 辛愛佯發兵，陰擇便利，以故俺答不得誌。

translations.literal: Senge pretended to march out but secretly chose advantageous ground, so that Altan Khan could not achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Senge feigned to deploy his men while secretly choosing the easier course, and thus Altan Khan failed to accomplish his purpose.

sentences.zh: 一克哈屯思其孫，朝夕哭，俺答患之。

translations.literal: Ikhai Khatun yearned for her grandson and wept morning and night; Altan Khan was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Ikhai Khatun, longing for her grandson, wept day and night until Altan Khan grew vexed.

sentences.zh: 巡撫逢時遣百戶鮑崇德入其營，俺答盛氣待之曰：「自吾用兵，而鎮將多死。」

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Fang Fengshi sent centurion Bao Chongde into the Mongol camp; Altan Khan received him in full wrath and said, "Since I took up arms, many frontier commanders have died."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Fang Fengshi sent Centurion Bao Chongde into the camp. Altan Khan met him in a fury and said, "Since I took up arms, how many frontier commanders have perished."

sentences.zh: 崇德曰：「鎮將孰與而孫？

translations.literal: Bao Chongde said, "How do those commanders compare with your grandson?
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chongde replied, "What are those commanders beside your grandson?

sentences.zh: 今朝廷待而孫甚厚，稱兵是速其死也。」

translations.literal: The court now treats your grandson with great favor; to raise arms is to hasten his death."
translations.idiomatic: The court treats your grandson with the utmost favor. To march against us is to hasten his death."

sentences.zh: 俺答疑把漢已死，及聞言，心動，使使诇之。

translations.literal: Altan Khan suspected Batahan was already dead; when he heard this, his heart wavered, and he sent men to spy out the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan had feared Batahan was already dead; at these words his heart stirred, and he sent envoys to investigate.

sentences.zh: 崇古令把漢緋袍金帶見使者，俺答喜過望，崇德因說之曰：「趙全等旦至，把漢夕返。」

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu had Batahan appear before the envoys in scarlet robe and gold belt; Altan Khan was delighted beyond expectation, and Bao Chongde thereupon urged him, saying, "Zhao Quan and the rest will arrive by morning, and Batahan will return by evening."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu had Batahan greet the envoys in scarlet robe and gold belt. Altan Khan rejoiced beyond all hope. Bao Chongde pressed him: "Deliver Zhao Quan and his fellows by dawn, and Batahan returns by dusk."

sentences.zh: 俺答大喜，屏人語曰：「我不為亂，亂由全等。

translations.literal: Altan Khan was greatly pleased, dismissed those present, and said in private, "I did not seek disorder; disorder came from Zhao Quan and his ilk.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan was overjoyed. Dismissing attendants, he said privately, "I did not seek turmoil—turmoil came from Zhao Quan and his gang.

sentences.zh: 令吾孫降漢，是天遣之合也。

translations.literal: That my grandson should submit to the Han is Heaven's own accord.
translations.idiomatic: That my grandson should submit to the Han is Heaven's own design.

sentences.zh: 天子幸封我為王，永長北方，諸部孰敢為患。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has graciously enfeoffed me as king to rule the north forever—what tribe would dare make trouble?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has deigned to enfeoff me king of the north for all time—what tribe would dare trouble me?

sentences.zh: 即不幸死，我孫當襲封，彼受朝廷厚恩，豈敢負耶？」

translations.literal: Even if I should die untimely, my grandson will inherit the enfeoffment; having received the court's great grace, how would he dare betray it?"
translations.idiomatic: Should I die before my time, my grandson will inherit the title. Having tasted the court's bounty, how could he turn traitor?"

sentences.zh: 遂遣使與崇德俱來，又為辛愛求官，並請互市。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to come with Bao Chongde, also sought an office for Senge, and requested mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys with Bao Chongde, interceded for an office for Senge, and asked for border markets.

sentences.zh: 崇古以聞，帝悉報可。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu reported this; the Emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu reported upward; the Emperor approved every request.

sentences.zh: 俺答遂縛全等十余人以獻，崇古亦遣使送把漢歸。

translations.literal: Altan Khan then bound Zhao Quan and more than ten others and presented them; Wang Chonggu also sent envoys to return Batahan.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan bound Zhao Quan and a dozen others and sent them as tribute. Wang Chonggu, in turn, returned Batahan by envoy.

sentences.zh: 帝以叛人既得，祭告郊廟，磔全等於市。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having secured the rebels, offered sacrifice to inform the suburban altars and dismembered Zhao Quan and the rest in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: With the traitors in hand, the Emperor reported to the suburban altars and had Zhao Quan and his fellows torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 加崇古太子少保、兵部尚書，總督如故。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, retaining his post as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War while remaining supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 把漢既歸，俺答與其妻撫之泣。

translations.literal: After Batahan returned, Altan Khan and his wife embraced him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Batahan came home, Altan Khan and his wife held him and wept.

sentences.zh: 遣使報謝，誓不犯大同。

translations.literal: He sent envoys with thanks and swore not to violate Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys carried his thanks, and he swore never again to strike at Datong.

sentences.zh: 崇古令要土蠻、昆都力、吉能等皆入貢，俺答報如約，惟土蠻不至。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu required Tumen, Kunultu, Jining, and the rest all to present tribute; Altan Khan answered that they would comply as agreed—only Tumen did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu demanded tribute from Tumen, Kunultu, Jining, and the rest. Altan Khan pledged compliance, but Tumen alone stayed away.

sentences.zh: 崇古念土蠻勢孤，薊、昌可無患，命將士勿燒荒搗巢，議通貢市，休息邊民。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu reckoned that with Tumen isolated, Ji and Chang could be free of worry; he ordered officers and men not to burn the steppe or raid camps, and proposed opening tribute and trade to let the border people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Tumen isolated and Ji and Chang therefore secure, Wang Chonggu forbade burning the grasslands or raiding camps, and urged tribute and markets so the frontier people might breathe.

sentences.zh: 朝議復嘩。

translations.literal: Court debate erupted again.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate flared anew.

sentences.zh: 尚書郭乾謂馬市先帝明禁，不宜許。

translations.literal: Minister Guo Qian said the horse markets were expressly forbidden by the late emperor and ought not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Guo Qian argued that the late emperor had expressly forbidden horse markets and they must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 給事中章端甫請敕崇古無邀近功，忽遠慮。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Duanfu asked that Wang Chonggu be instructed not to grasp at immediate gain and neglect far-sighted care.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Duanfu asked that Wang Chonggu be charged not to seize a near triumph and forget distant peril.

sentences.zh: 崇古上疏曰：「先帝既誅仇鸞，制復言開市者斬，邊臣何敢故違禁旨，自陷重辟。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu memorialized, saying, "After the late emperor executed Qiu Luan, he decreed death for anyone who again spoke of opening markets—how would a frontier official dare deliberately defy the prohibition and court the gravest penalty?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu memorialized: "After the late emperor executed Qiu Luan, he decreed death for anyone who spoke again of opening markets. What frontier officer would deliberately defy that and invite execution?

sentences.zh: 但敵勢既異昔強，我兵亦非昔怯，不當援以為例。

translations.literal: Yet the enemy's strength is no longer what it was, and our troops are no longer as timid as before; the old case should not be invoked.
translations.idiomatic: But the enemy is no longer as strong as then, nor our troops as timid. The old precedent should not bind us.

sentences.zh: 夫先帝禁開馬市，未禁北敵之納款。

translations.literal: The late emperor forbade opening horse markets; he did not forbid the northern enemy's submission.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor forbade horse markets, not the submission of northern foes.

sentences.zh: 今敵求貢市，不過如遼東、開原、廣寧之規，商人自以有無貿易，非請復開馬市也。

translations.literal: What the enemy now seeks in tribute and trade is merely the practice of Liaodong, Kaiyuan, and Guangning—merchants trading as they have goods or not; this is not a request to reopen horse markets.
translations.idiomatic: What they seek is merely the Liaodong, Kaiyuan, and Guangning arrangement—merchants trading what they have. It is not a demand to reopen horse markets.

sentences.zh: 俺答父子兄弟橫行四五十年，震驚宸嚴，流毒畿輔，莫收遏劉功者，緣議論太多，文網牽制，使邊臣無所措手足耳。

translations.literal: For forty or fifty years Altan Khan, his sons and brothers, rampaged unchecked, shaking the imperial precincts and poisoning the capital region; none could restrain them or win credit for doing so, because debate was endless and paperwork bound the frontier officials until they could not move hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: For forty or fifty years Altan Khan and his kin rampaged, shaking the throne and poisoning the capital approaches, yet none could check them or claim victory—because endless debate and bureaucratic nets left frontier officers unable to act.

sentences.zh: 昨秋，俺答東行，京師戒嚴，至倡運磚聚灰塞門乘城之計。

translations.literal: Last autumn, when Altan Khan marched east, the capital went on alert, even to proposals of hauling bricks, heaping ash to block gates, and manning the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn Altan marched east. Beijing went on alert, even to hauling bricks, piling ash to block gates, and crowding the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 今納款求貢，又必責以久要，欲保百年無事，否則治首事之罪。

translations.literal: Now that they submit and seek tribute, we must again demand long-term pledges and expect a century without incident, or else punish those who took the first step.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they submit and seek tribute, we demand eternal pledges and a century of peace—or else punish the men who led the way.

sentences.zh: 豈惟臣等不能逆料，他時雖俺答亦恐能保其身，不能制諸部於身後也。

translations.literal: Not only can we ministers not foresee the future—even Altan Khan himself may be able to preserve his own life yet unable to control the tribes after his death.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers cannot foresee the future; nor, in time, may Altan Khan himself guarantee control of the tribes once he is gone.

sentences.zh: 夫拒敵甚易，執先帝禁旨，一言可決。

translations.literal: To refuse the enemy is very easy: uphold the late emperor's prohibition, and one word settles it.
translations.idiomatic: Refusal is easy: invoke the late emperor's ban and decide with a word.

sentences.zh: 但敵既不得請，懷憤而去，縱以把漢之故，不擾宣、大，而土蠻三衛歲窺薊、遼，吉能、賓兔侵擾西鄙，息警無時，財務殫絀，雖智者無以善其後矣。

translations.literal: But if the enemy, denied their request, depart in resentment, then even if, for Batahan's sake, they do not trouble Xuan and Da, Tumen and the three guards will yearly spy on Ji and Liao, Jining and Bintu will harass the western marches, alarms will never cease, and finances will be exhausted—no wise man could mend matters afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if they are refused and leave in wrath, then even if, for Batahan's sake, they spare Xuan and Da, Tumen and the three guards will harry Ji and Liao yearly, Jining and Bintu the western marches. Alarms will never end and the treasury will bleed dry—no sage could repair what follows.

sentences.zh: 昔也先以克減馬價而稱兵，忠順王以元裔而封哈密，小王子由大同二年三貢，此皆前代封貢故事。

translations.literal: In former times Esen took up arms over reduced horse prices; the Loyal and Obedient Prince was enfeoffed at Hami as a Yuan descendant; the Little Prince thrice presented tribute through Datong in two years—all precedents of enfeoffment and tribute from earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Esen once marched over reduced horse prices; the Loyal and Obedient Prince was enfeoffed at Hami as a Yuan scion; the Little Prince thrice offered tribute through Datong in two years—all precedents of enfeoffment and tribute.

sentences.zh: 夫揆之時勢，既當俯從，考之典故，非今創始。

translations.literal: Measured against the times, we ought to yield; measured against precedent, this is no innovation of today.
translations.idiomatic: The times demand compliance; precedent shows this is no invention of our day.

sentences.zh: 堂堂天朝，容荒服之來王，昭聖圖之廣大，以示東西諸部，傳天下萬世，諸臣何疑憚而不為耶？」

translations.literal: The august Celestial Dynasty may receive kings from the wild borderlands, displaying the breadth of sacred dominion to all tribes east and west for ten thousand generations—why should ministers doubt and shrink from acting?"
translations.idiomatic: Let the august dynasty receive kings from the wilds, display the breadth of sacred rule to every tribe, and bequeath the example to ten thousand generations—why should ministers hesitate?"

sentences.zh: 因條封貢八事以上。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth eight points on enfeoffment and tribute and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted eight articles on enfeoffment and tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔下廷議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the matter to court debate.

sentences.zh: 定國公徐文璧、侍郎張四維以下二十二人以為可許，英國公張溶、尚書張守直以下十七人以為不可許。

translations.literal: Duke of Dingguo Xu Wenbi, Vice Minister Zhang Siwei, and twenty-two others held it permissible; Duke of Yingguo Zhang Rong, Minister Zhang Shouzhi, and seventeen others held it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dingguo Xu Wenbi, Vice Minister Zhang Siwei, and twenty-two others favored approval; Duke of Yingguo Zhang Rong, Minister Zhang Shouzhi, and seventeen others opposed it.

sentences.zh: 尚書朱衡等五人言封貢便、互市不便，獨僉都御史李棠極言當許狀。

translations.literal: Ministers Zhu Heng and five others said enfeoffment and tribute were expedient but mutual markets not; only Censor-in-Chief Li Tang strongly argued that submission ought to be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhu Heng and five colleagues favored tribute but not markets; only Censor-in-Chief Li Tang urged acceptance in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 郭乾悉上眾議。

translations.literal: Guo Qian reported all opinions to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qian reported every opinion to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會帝御經筵，閣臣面請外示羈縻，內修守備。

translations.literal: As the Emperor attended the classics lecture, the Grand Secretaries asked in person to show loose reins outward while strengthening defense within.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics lecture the Grand Secretaries asked that outward show be one of loose reins, inward policy one of hard defense.

sentences.zh: 乃詔封俺答順義王，名所居城曰歸化；

translations.literal: An edict then enfeoffed Altan Khan as Prince of Shunyi and named his city Guihua, "Return to Transformation";
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Altan Khan as Prince of Shunyi and named his seat Guihua—Return to Transformation;

sentences.zh: 昆都力、辛愛等皆授官；

translations.literal: Kunultu, Senge, and the rest were all granted offices;
translations.idiomatic: Kunultu, Senge, and the rest received offices;

sentences.zh: 封把漢昭勇將軍，指揮使如故。

translations.literal: Batahan was enfeoffed General of Manifest Courage, retaining his post as battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: Batahan was made General of Manifest Courage while keeping his battalion command.

sentences.zh: 俺答率諸部受詔甚恭，使使貢馬，執趙全余黨以獻。

translations.literal: Altan Khan led the tribes to receive the edict with great respect, sent envoys presenting horses, and delivered the remaining partisans of Zhao Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan led the tribes to receive the edict with deep respect, sent horses in tribute, and handed over Zhao Quan's remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其誠，賜金幣。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his sincerity and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his sincerity and rewarded him with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 又雜采崇古及廷臣議，賜王印，給食用，加撫賞，惟貢使不聽入京。

translations.literal: Further adopting proposals of Wang Chonggu and court officials, he granted the princely seal, supplied provisions, added pacification gifts, but did not allow tribute envoys into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting proposals from Wang Chonggu and the court, he granted the princely seal and provisions, added pacification gifts, but barred tribute envoys from the capital.

sentences.zh: 河套吉能亦如約請命。

translations.literal: Jining of the Ordos likewise asked for orders according to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Jining of the Ordos likewise petitioned for enfeoffment under the agreement.

sentences.zh: 以事在陜西，下總督王之誥議。

translations.literal: Because the matter lay in Shaanxi, it was referred to Supreme Commander Wang Zhigao for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Because the matter lay in Shaanxi, it went to Supreme Commander Wang Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 之誥欲令吉能一二年不犯，方許封貢。

translations.literal: Wang Zhigao wished to require that Jining commit no raids for a year or two before enfeoffment and tribute were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhigao wanted two years without raids before granting enfeoffment and tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇古復上疏曰：「俺答、吉能親為叔侄，首尾相應。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu memorialized again, saying, "Altan Khan and Jining are uncle and nephew in fact, acting head and tail in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu memorialized again: "Altan Khan and Jining are uncle and nephew in truth, acting in concert head and tail.

sentences.zh: 今收其叔而縱其侄，錮其首而舒其臂，俺答必呼吉能之眾就市河東宣、大；

translations.literal: Now to embrace the uncle and loose the nephew is to fetter the head and free the arm; Altan Khan will surely summon Jining's followers to trade east of the river in Xuan and Da;
translations.idiomatic: To embrace the uncle and loose the nephew is to bind the head and free the arm. Altan will summon Jining's people to market east of the river in Xuan and Da;

sentences.zh: 商販不能給，而吉能糾俺答擾陜西，四鎮之憂方大矣。」
