translations.literal: merchants cannot supply them all, and Jining will rally Altan Khan to trouble Shaanxi—the worry of the four garrisons will then be great indeed."
translations.idiomatic: Merchants cannot supply them all, and Jining will rally Altan to ravage Shaanxi—the four garrisons will face far greater peril."

sentences.zh: 帝然其言，亦授吉能都督同知。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his reasoning and likewise appointed Jining Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and likewise made Jining Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 崇古乃廣召商販，聽令貿易。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu then broadly summoned merchants and permitted trade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu then summoned merchants broadly and opened trade.

sentences.zh: 布帛、菽粟、皮革遠自江淮、湖廣輻輳塞下，因收其稅以充犒賞。

translations.literal: Cloth, grain, and hides converged on the frontier from as far as the Yangtze-Huai and Huguang; he collected taxes on them to fund rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth, grain, and hides streamed to the passes from the Yangtze-Huai and Huguang, and he taxed them to fund rewards.

sentences.zh: 其大小部長則官給金繒，歲市馬各有數。

translations.literal: For great and small chieftains the government gave silks; yearly horse purchases were fixed in number.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small chiefs received silks from the state; annual horse purchases were fixed by quota.

sentences.zh: 崇古仍歲詣弘賜堡宣諭威德。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu still went yearly to Hongci Fort to proclaim imperial majesty and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Each year Wang Chonggu went to Hongci Fort to proclaim imperial majesty and grace.

sentences.zh: 諸部羅拜，無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: The tribes bowed in ranks; none dared make uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes bowed in ranks; none dared raise a clamor.

sentences.zh: 自是邊境休息。

translations.literal: From this the frontier knew rest.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the frontier knew rest.

sentences.zh: 東起延、永，西抵嘉峪七鎮，數千里軍民樂業，不用兵革，歲省費什七。

translations.literal: From Yan and Yong in the east to Jiayu in the west, across seven garrisons and thousands of li, soldiers and civilians rejoiced in their work, arms were not used, and yearly costs were cut by seven-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: From Yan and Yong east to Jiayu west, seven garrisons over thousands of li—soldiers and civilians at peace, arms unused, yearly costs cut by seven parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 詔進太子太保。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，召理戎政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he was summoned to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he was summoned to oversee military affairs.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉鉉劾崇古行賄營遷，詔責鉉妄言。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Xuan impeached Wang Chonggu for bribery to secure promotion; an edict rebuked Liu Xuan for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Xuan accused Wang Chonggu of bribery to win promotion; an edict rebuked Liu for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 已，加少保，遷刑部尚書，改兵部。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was made Junior Guardian, transferred to Minister of Punishments, then shifted to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian, then Minister of Punishments, then Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 初，俺答諸部嘗越甘肅掠西番。

translations.literal: Earlier, Altan Khan's tribes had crossed Gansu to raid the western Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Altan's tribes had crossed Gansu to raid the western Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 既通款，其從孫切盡臺吉連歲盜番，不得誌，求俺答西援。

translations.literal: After peace was opened, his grand-nephew Ciejin Taiji raided the Tibetans year after year without success and sought Altan Khan's aid to the west.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, his grand-nephew Ciejin Taiji raided Tibetans yearly without success and begged Altan's aid to the west.

sentences.zh: 崇古每作書止之，俺答亦報書謝。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu wrote repeatedly to restrain him; Altan Khan also answered with letters of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu wrote repeatedly to restrain him; Altan answered with thanks.

sentences.zh: 是年，俺答請與三鎮通事約誓，欲西迎佛。

translations.literal: That year Altan Khan asked to exchange envoys and oaths with the three garrisons, wishing to go west to welcome the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: That year Altan asked to exchange envoys and oaths with the three garrisons, intending to go west to welcome the Buddha.

sentences.zh: 崇古上言：「西行非俺答意，且以迎佛為名，不可沮，宜飭邊鎮嚴守備，而陰泄其謀於番族以示恩。」

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu reported, "The journey west is not Altan Khan's true aim; since he takes welcoming the Buddha as his pretext, we should not discourage him openly, but should order the garrisons to tighten defense while secretly revealing his design to the Tibetan tribes to show favor."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu reported: "The westward march is not Altan's true aim. Since he takes welcoming the Buddha as pretext, do not openly discourage him; tighten the garrisons while secretly warning the Tibetan tribes to show favor."

sentences.zh: 於是鉉及同官彭應時、南京御史陳堂交章論崇古弛防徇敵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Xuan, his colleague Peng Yingshi, and Nanjing Censor Chen Tang submitted successive memorials accusing Wang Chonggu of relaxing defense and favoring the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, Peng Yingshi, and Nanjing Censor Chen Tang then impeached Wang Chonggu for slackening defense and indulging the enemy.

sentences.zh: 崇古疏辯乞休。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu memorialized in defense and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu defended himself and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔報之，令勿以人言介意。

translations.literal: The Emperor answered with a gracious edict, telling him not to heed men's words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor answered graciously, bidding him pay no heed to gossip.

sentences.zh: 給事中尹瑾、御史高維崧再劾之，崇古力請致仕，帝乃允歸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Yin Jin and Censor Gao Weisong impeached him again; Wang Chonggu earnestly begged to resign, and the Emperor then permitted him to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jin and Censor Gao Weisong impeached him again. Wang Chonggu pressed hard for retirement, and the Emperor let him go.

sentences.zh: 俺答既死，辛愛、撦力克相繼襲封。

translations.literal: After Altan Khan died, Senge and Chelik succeeded to the enfeoffment in turn.
translations.idiomatic: After Altan died, Senge and Chelik succeeded to the title in turn.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔以崇古竭忠首事，三封告成，蔭一子世錦衣千戶，有司以禮存問。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict cited Wang Chonggu's exhausting loyalty in initiating the affair, the completion of the three enfeoffments, granted hereditary appointment of one son as commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and ordered the officials to visit him with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen an edict praised Wang Chonggu's loyal initiative in the three enfeoffments, granted one son hereditary command in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and ordered officials to visit him with ritual courtesy.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚襄毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Xiangyi, "Assisting and Resolute."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Xiangyi—Assisting and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 崇古身歷七鎮，勛著邊陲。

translations.literal: Wang Chonggu personally served seven garrisons; his merit shone on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chonggu served seven garrisons in person; his merit shone on the marches.

sentences.zh: 封貢之初，廷議紛呶，有為危言撼帝者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of enfeoffment and tribute, court debate was clamorous; some used alarming words to shake the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When enfeoffment and tribute began, court debate was fierce; some used alarming words to shake the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 閣臣力持之，乃得成功。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretaries held firm, and success was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretaries held firm, and success followed.

sentences.zh: 順義歸款二十年，崇古乃歿。

translations.literal: Twenty years of Shunyi's submission to grace passed before Wang Chonggu died.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years of Shunyi's submission passed before Wang Chonggu died.

sentences.zh: 總督梅友松撫馭失宜，西邊始擾，而禍已紓於嘉靖時，宣、大則歸款迄明季不變。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Mei Yousong governed improperly and the western marches began to be troubled, yet the calamity had already been eased in the Jiajing era; Xuan and Da maintained submission until the dynasty's end.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme Commander Mei Yousong mismanaged affairs and the west grew troubled again, yet the worst had been eased in Jiajing; Xuan and Da kept the peace until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 子謙，萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: His son Qian passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian became a metropolitan graduate in Wanli year five.

sentences.zh: 官工部主事，榷稅杭州。

translations.literal: He served as secretary in the Ministry of Works and collected transit duties at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretary in the Ministry of Works and levied transit duties at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 羅木營兵變，脅執巡撫吳善言。

translations.literal: When the Luomu camp mutinied, the soldiers seized Grand Coordinator Wu Shanyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Luomu garrison mutinied, the troops seized Grand Coordinator Wu Shanyan.

sentences.zh: 謙馳諭之乃解。

translations.literal: Qian galloped to instruct them, and only then were they released.
translations.idiomatic: Qian rode in haste to reason with them, and the hostage was freed.

sentences.zh: 終太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 孫之楨，以蔭累官太子太保、左都督，掌錦衣衛事凡十有七年；

translations.literal: His grandson Zhizhen, by hereditary privilege, rose to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Chief Commander, directing the Embroidered Uniform Guard for seventeen years altogether;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhizhen, by privilege of descent, rose to Grand Guardian and Left Chief Commander, directing the Embroidered Uniform Guard for seventeen years;

sentences.zh: 之采，萬歷二十六年進士，官兵部右侍郎，陜西三邊總督。

translations.literal: Zhicai, metropolitan graduate in Wanli year twenty-six, served as Vice Minister of War and supreme commander of the three western garrisons of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicai, a Wanli year-twenty-six graduate, became Vice Minister of War and supreme commander of Shaanxi's three western garrisons.

sentences.zh: 李棠，長沙人。

translations.literal: Li Tang was a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang was from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 由吏部郎中累遷右副都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: From a director in the Ministry of Personnel he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: From director in the Ministry of Personnel he rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 督僉事諸察討平韶州山賊。

translations.literal: As supervising commissioner he joined the pacification and subdued the mountain bandits of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising commissioner he joined campaigns and pacified the mountain bandits of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 終南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 仕宦三十年，以介潔稱。

translations.literal: For thirty years in office he was known for integrity and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years in office won him a name for integrity and austerity.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚恭懿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously given the name Gongyi, "Reverent and Gracious."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he received the posthumous name Gongyi—Reverent and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 方逢時，字行之，嘉魚人。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi, styled Xingzhi, was a native of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi, styled Xingzhi, was from Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in Jiajing year twenty.

sentences.zh: 授宜興知縣，再徙寧津、曲周。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yixing, then transferred to Ningjin and Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yixing, then moved to Ningjin and Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部主事，歷工部郎中，遷寧國知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, served as director in the Ministry of Works, and was transferred to prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretary in Revenue, served as director in Works, and became prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 廣東、江西盜起，詔於興寧、程鄉、安遠、武平間築伸威鎮，擢逢時廣東兵備副使，與參將俞大猷鎮之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Guangdong and Jiangxi, an edict ordered Shenwei Garrison built between Xingning, Chengxiang, Anyuan, and Wuping; Fang Fengshi was promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner for military preparedness and, with Regional Commander Yu Dayou, garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Guangdong and Jiangxi, an edict built Shenwei Garrison between Xingning, Chengxiang, Anyuan, and Wuping. Fang Fengshi was made Guangdong vice commissioner for military preparedness and garrisoned it with Regional Commander Yu Dayou.

sentences.zh: 已而程鄉賊平，移巡惠州。

translations.literal: When the Chengxiang bandits were pacified, he was moved to inspect Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengxiang bandits were pacified, he was shifted to inspect Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，改宣府口北道，加右參政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was shifted to the North Pass circuit of Xuanfu and made Right Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing he took the Xuanfu North Pass circuit as Right Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，移大同。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was transferred to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four he was transferred to Datong.

sentences.zh: 俺答犯威遠堡，別部千余騎攻靖鹵，伏兵卻之。

translations.literal: Altan Khan attacked Weiyuan Fort; another division of more than a thousand horsemen struck Jinglu, and ambush troops drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Altan struck Weiyuan Fort; another column of a thousand horse attacked Jinglu and was repelled by ambush.

sentences.zh: 其冬，俺答孫把漢那吉來降，逢時告總督王崇古曰：「機不可失也。」

translations.literal: That winter Altan Khan's grandson Batahan Nangji came to submit; Fang Fengshi told Supreme Commander Wang Chonggu, "The opportunity must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: That winter Altan's grandson Batahan Nangji surrendered. Fang Fengshi told Wang Chonggu, "The moment must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 遣中軍康綸率騎五百往受之。

translations.literal: He sent his central commander Kang Lun with five hundred horse to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Central Commander Kang Lun with five hundred cavalry to receive him.

sentences.zh: 與崇古定計，挾把漢以索叛人趙全等。

translations.literal: With Wang Chonggu he settled on a plan to use Batahan as leverage to demand the traitors Zhao Quan and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Chonggu he planned to use Batahan as leverage to demand the traitor Zhao Quan and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 遣百戶鮑崇德出雲石堡語俺答部下五奴柱曰：「欲還把漢則速納款，若以兵來，是趣之死矣。」

translations.literal: He sent centurion Bao Chongde out from Yunshi Fort to tell Altan Khan's subordinate Wunuzhu, "If you wish Batahan returned, submit quickly; if you come with troops, you hasten his death."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Centurion Bao Chongde from Yunshi Fort to tell Altan's man Wunuzhu: "Return Batahan at once by submitting. March with arms and you hasten his death."

sentences.zh: 五奴柱白俺答，邀入營，說以執趙全易把漢。

translations.literal: Wunuzhu reported to Altan Khan, invited Bao into camp, and urged handing over Zhao Quan in exchange for Batahan.
translations.idiomatic: Wunuzhu reported to Altan, invited Bao into camp, and urged seizing Zhao Quan in exchange for Batahan.

sentences.zh: 俺答心動，遣火力赤致書逢時。

translations.literal: Altan Khan's heart stirred; he sent Huolichi with a letter to Fang Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Altan's heart stirred; he sent Huolichi with a letter to Fang Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 而全方從臾用兵，俺答又惑之，令其子辛愛將二萬騎入弘賜堡，兄子永邵卜趨威遠堡，自率眾犯平虜城。

translations.literal: But Zhao Quan was then urging war, and Altan Khan was swayed again; he ordered his son Senge to lead twenty thousand horse into Hongci Fort, his brother's son Yongshabuo toward Weiyuan Fort, and himself led the host against Pinglu City.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhao Quan was urging war, and Altan wavered again. He sent Senge with twenty thousand horse against Hongci Fort, his brother's son Yongshabuo toward Weiyuan, and led the main host against Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 逢時曰：「此必趙全謀也。」

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi said, "This must be Zhao Quan's plot."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi said, "This is surely Zhao Quan's doing."

sentences.zh: 全嘗投書逢時，言悔禍思漢，欲復歸中國。

translations.literal: Zhao Quan had once sent Fang Fengshi a letter saying he repented his calamity and yearned for the Han, wishing to return to China.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Quan had once written Fang Fengshi that he repented and wished to return to China.

sentences.zh: 逢時以示俺答，俺答大驚，有執全意。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi showed it to Altan Khan; Altan Khan was greatly alarmed and inclined to seize Zhao Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi showed it to Altan, who was greatly alarmed and inclined to seize Zhao Quan.

sentences.zh: 及戰，又不利，乃引退。

translations.literal: When battle went against him again, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When battle went ill, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛愛猶未知，奄至大同。

translations.literal: Senge still did not know and suddenly arrived at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Senge, still unaware, suddenly appeared at Datong.

sentences.zh: 逢時使人持把漢箭示之曰：「吾已與而父約，以報汝。」

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi had a man show him Batahan's arrow and say, "I have already made a pact with your father to answer you."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi sent a man with Batahan's arrow, saying, "I have already pledged with your father to answer you."

sentences.zh: 辛愛執箭泣曰：「此吾弟鐵背臺吉故物也，我來求把漢，把漢既授官，又有成約，當更計之。」

translations.literal: Senge took the arrow and wept, saying, "This was my younger brother Iron-back Taiji's possession. I came seeking Batahan; Batahan has already been given an office and there is a settled agreement—we must reconsider."
translations.idiomatic: Senge gripped the arrow and wept. "This was my brother Iron-back Taiji's. I came for Batahan; he already holds office and a pact is made—we must think again."

sentences.zh: 乃遣部下啞都善入見。

translations.literal: He then sent his subordinate Yadushan to enter and be received.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his follower Yadushan to audience.

sentences.zh: 逢時曉以大義，犒而遣之。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi instructed him in the larger principle, rewarded him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi instructed him in duty, feasted him, and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 辛愛喜，因使求幣，逢時笑曰：「臺吉，豪傑也，若納款，方重加爵賞，何愛此區區，損盛名。」

translations.literal: Senge was pleased and then sent to ask for silks; Fang Fengshi laughed and said, "Taiji, you are a hero; if you submit, you will be richly enfeoffed and rewarded—why cherish this trifle and stain your great name?"
translations.idiomatic: Senge rejoiced and asked for silks. Fang Fengshi laughed: "Taiji, you are a hero. Submit and you will be richly enfeoffed—why haggle over trifles and stain your name?"

sentences.zh: 辛愛大慚，復遣啞都善來謝曰：「邊人不知書，蒙太師教，幸甚。

translations.literal: Senge was deeply ashamed and again sent Yadushan to thank him, saying, "We border people do not know letters; to receive the Grand Coordinator's instruction is our great fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply ashamed, Senge sent Yadushan again: "We border folk are unlettered. Your instruction, Grand Coordinator, is our fortune.

sentences.zh: 俺答使者至故將田世威所，世威亦讓之曰：「爾來求和，兵何為者？」

translations.literal: Altan Khan's envoys came to former general Tian Shiwei's post; Tian Shiwei also reproved them, saying, "You come seeking peace—why then troops?"
translations.idiomatic: Altan's envoys came to former general Tian Shiwei, who reproved them: "You seek peace—why then arms?"

sentences.zh: 使者還報俺答，召辛愛還。

translations.literal: The envoys returned and reported to Altan Khan, who recalled Senge.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys reported back; Altan recalled Senge.

sentences.zh: 辛愛東行，宣府總兵官趙岢遏之，復由大同北去。

translations.literal: Senge marched east; Xuanfu supreme commander Zhao Ke blocked him, and he went north again through Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Senge marched east; Xuanfu commander Zhao Ke blocked him, and he turned north again through Datong.

sentences.zh: 於是巡按御史姚繼可劾逢時輒通寇使，屏人語，導之東行，嫁禍鄰鎮。

translations.literal: Thereupon Investigating Censor Yao Jike impeached Fang Fengshi for casually receiving enemy envoys, speaking with them in private, guiding them eastward, and shifting blame onto neighboring garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Yao Jike then impeached Fang Fengshi for receiving enemy envoys freely, speaking in private, guiding them east, and shifting blame to neighboring garrisons.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱曰：「撫臣臨機設策，何可泄也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gong said, "A grand coordinator sets stratagems on the spot—how can that be disclosed?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gong said, "A grand coordinator shapes stratagems in the moment—how can that be disclosed beforehand?

sentences.zh: 但當觀後效，不宜先事輒易。」

translations.literal: One should watch the outcome; one should not lightly change course beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Watch the outcome; do not lightly change course before the fact."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 俺答乃遣使定約，夜召全等計事，即帳中縛之送大同。

translations.literal: Altan Khan then sent envoys to fix the agreement; by night he summoned Zhao Quan and the rest to discuss affairs and bound them in the tent, sending them to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Altan sent envoys to fix terms, summoned Zhao Quan and his fellows by night, bound them in the tent, and sent them to Datong.

sentences.zh: 逢時受之，崇古亦送把漢歸。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi received them; Wang Chonggu also sent Batahan back.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi received them; Wang Chonggu returned Batahan.

sentences.zh: 逢時以功進兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史。

translations.literal: For his merit Fang Fengshi was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Fang Fengshi was made Vice Minister of War and Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 甫拜命，以憂歸。

translations.literal: He had just received the appointment when mourning called him home.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely accepted the appointment when mourning called him home.

sentences.zh: 後崇古入理京營，神宗問誰可代者，大學士張居正以逢時對。

translations.literal: Later, when Wang Chonggu entered the capital to manage the metropolitan garrison, Shenzong asked who could replace him; Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng named Fang Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Chonggu took charge of the capital garrisons, Shenzong asked who might replace him. Zhang Juzheng named Fang Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，起故官，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was recalled to his former rank and made supreme commander of the military affairs of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he was recalled and made supreme commander of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 始逢時與崇古共決大計，而貢市之議崇古獨成之。

translations.literal: At first Fang Fengshi and Wang Chonggu together settled the great plan, but the policy of tribute and markets Wang Chonggu alone brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fang Fengshi and Wang Chonggu settled the grand design together, but Wang Chonggu alone carried tribute and markets through.

sentences.zh: 逢時復代崇古，乃申明約信。

translations.literal: When Fang Fengshi again replaced Wang Chonggu, he clarified the covenants of trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Fengshi succeeded Wang Chonggu, he renewed the covenants of trust.

sentences.zh: 兩人首尾共濟，邊境遂安。

translations.literal: The two men worked head and tail in concert, and the frontier was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Working in concert from first to last, they secured the frontier.

sentences.zh: 逢時分巡口北，時親行塞外，自龍門盤道墩以東至靖湖堡山梁一百餘里，形勢聯絡，嘆曰：「此山天險。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi inspected the North Pass in person, often traveling beyond the wall; from Longmen Pandao Beacon east to the ridge at Jinghu Fort, more than a hundred li of terrain linked together, and he sighed, "This mountain is heaven's barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi inspected the North Pass in person, often riding beyond the wall. From Longmen Pandao Beacon east to the Jinghu ridge—over a hundred li of linked terrain—he sighed, "This ridge is heaven's barrier.

sentences.zh: 若修鑿，北可達獨石，南可援南山，誠陵京一藩籬也。」

translations.literal: If cut and opened, northward one could reach Dushi, southward aid the Southern Mountains—truly a screen for the imperial tombs and the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Cut a road through it and one could reach Dushi north and aid the Southern Mountains south—a true screen for the tombs and the capital."

sentences.zh: 及赴陽和，道居庸，出關見邊務修舉，欲並遂前計。

translations.literal: When he went to Yanghe, passed Juyong, and went out through the pass to see frontier works well maintained, he wished to carry out the earlier plan as well.
translations.idiomatic: Going to Yanghe by Juyong, he saw the frontier well ordered and wished to carry the plan through.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「獨石在宣府北，三面鄰敵，勢極孤懸。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying, "Dushi lies north of Xuanfu, bordered on three sides by the enemy, extremely isolated and exposed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Dushi lies north of Xuanfu, enemy on three sides, perilously exposed.

sentences.zh: 懷、永與陵寢止限一山，所系尤重。

translations.literal: Huai and Yong are separated from the imperial tombs by only one mountain range—the stake is especially grave.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Yong are separated from the imperial tombs by a single range—the stake is grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 其地本相屬，而經行之路尚在塞外，以故聲援不便。

translations.literal: The territories are naturally connected, yet the route of travel still lies outside the passes, so mutual support is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The lands are naturally joined, yet the road still lies beyond the passes, so mutual aid is slow.

sentences.zh: 若設盤道之險，舍迂就徑，自龍門黑峪以達寧遠，經行三十里，南山、獨石皆可朝發夕至，不惟拓地百里，亦可漸資屯牧，於戰守皆利。」

translations.literal: If the hazard of Pandao were opened, abandoning the circuitous for the direct, from Longmen Heiyu to Ningyuan in thirty li of travel, the Southern Mountains and Dushi could both be reached from dawn to dusk; not only would a hundred li of territory be expanded, gradual colonization and grazing could be supported—advantageous for both defense and attack."
translations.idiomatic: Open Pandao, cut the straight path from Longmen Heiyu to Ningyuan—thirty li—and Dushi and the Southern Mountains could answer each other within a day. We would expand a hundred li of ground and feed garrisons by colonization, to the good of defense and attack alike."

sentences.zh: 遂與巡撫吳兌經營修築，設兵戍守。

translations.literal: He then joined Grand Coordinator Wu Dui in planning construction and set troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand Coordinator Wu Dui in building the works and posting garrisons.

sentences.zh: 累進兵部尚書兼右副都御史，總督如故，加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Minister of War and Vice Censor-in-Chief, retaining his supreme command, and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of War and Vice Censor-in-Chief, kept supreme command, and was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，召理戎政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was summoned to manage military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議者爭言貢市利害，逢時臨赴闕，上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time debaters contended over the benefits and harms of tribute and markets; as Fang Fengshi was about to attend court, he memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Debate raged over tribute and markets. As Fang Fengshi prepared to attend court, he memorialized:

sentences.zh: 陛下特恩起臣草土中，代崇古任，賴陛下神武，八年以來，九邊生齒日繁，守備日固，田野日辟，商賈日通，邊民始知有生之樂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty graciously raised me from the soil to replace Wang Chonggu; relying on Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, in eight years the nine frontiers' population has daily grown, defenses daily strengthened, fields daily opened, merchants daily increased in traffic, and the border people have begun to know the joy of living.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty raised me from obscurity to replace Wang Chonggu. By your martial grace, in eight years the nine marches have grown in people, hardened in defense, widened in fields, and quickened in trade—the border folk have learned what it is to live.

sentences.zh: 北部輸誠效貢，莫敢渝約，歲時請求，隨宜與之，得一果餅，輒稽首歡笑。

translations.literal: The northern tribes offer sincerity and tribute, none daring break covenant; seasonal requests are met as fit—a single fruit cake wins bowed heads and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes offer loyalty and tribute and dare not break covenant. Meet their seasonal requests as fit—a fruit cake wins bowed heads and laughter.

sentences.zh: 有掠人要賞，如打喇明安兔者，告俺答罰治，即俯首聽命。

translations.literal: When there is plunder and demands for reward—as with Dalai Mingantu—report to Altan Khan for punishment, and they at once bow their heads in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders demand reward—as Dalai Mingantu did—complaint to Altan brings instant submission.

sentences.zh: 而異議者或曰「敵使充斥為害」，或曰「日益費耗，彼欲終不可足」，或曰「與寇益狎，隱憂叵測」。

translations.literal: Yet dissenters say, "Enemy envoys swarm and do harm," or "Costs mount daily and their desires can never be satisfied," or "Growing familiar with bandits breeds hidden worries beyond reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet critics say enemy envoys swarm and harm us, costs mount and appetites never end, or familiarity with raiders breeds hidden peril.

sentences.zh: 此言心則忠矣，事機或未睹也。

translations.literal: These words are loyal in heart, yet the turn of affairs may not have been seen.
translations.idiomatic: Their hearts are loyal, yet they may not see how affairs truly stand.

sentences.zh: 夫使者之入，多者八九人，少者二三人，朝至夕去，守貢之使，賞至即歸，何有充斥。

translations.literal: Envoys who enter are at most eight or nine, at least two or three; they arrive in the morning and leave by evening; envoys guarding tribute return as soon as reward is given—where is the swarm?
translations.idiomatic: Envoys number at most eight or nine, at least two or three. They come at dawn and leave at dusk; tribute guards return when rewarded—where is the swarm?

sentences.zh: 財貨之費，有市本，有撫賞，計三鎮歲費二十七萬，較之鄉時戶部客餉七十余萬，太仆馬價十數萬，十才二三耳。

translations.literal: Expenditure on goods includes market capital and pacification gifts; the three garrisons spend two hundred seventy thousand yearly—compared with former Ministry of Revenue guest rations of more than seven hundred thousand and Stud horse prices of more than one hundred thousand, barely two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Costs include market capital and pacification gifts—two hundred seventy thousand yearly for three garrisons, against former guest rations of seven hundred thousand and stud horse prices over one hundred thousand: barely two or three in ten.

sentences.zh: 而民間耕獲之入，市賈之利不與焉。

translations.literal: The gains of farming and harvest among the people, the profits of merchants—these are not counted.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is this to count farming gains and merchants' profits among the people.

sentences.zh: 所省甚多，何有耗費。

translations.literal: What is saved is very great—where is the drain?
translations.idiomatic: The savings are vast—where is the drain?

sentences.zh: 乃若所憂則有之，然非隱也。

translations.literal: As for what is to be feared, that exists—but it is not hidden.
translations.idiomatic: What is to be feared exists—but it is not hidden.

sentences.zh: 方庚午以前，三軍暴骨，萬姓流離，城郭丘墟，芻糧耗竭，邊臣首領不保，朝廷為旰食。

translations.literal: Before the gengwu year the three armies' bones lay exposed, the myriad people were displaced, walls and towns were ruins, fodder and grain were exhausted, frontier officers could not keep their heads, and the court ate late in worry.
translations.idiomatic: Before the gengwu year armies rotted on the field, people fled, walls crumbled, fodder failed, frontier officers lost their heads, and the court ate late in dread.

sentences.zh: 七八年來，幸無此事矣。

translations.literal: For seven or eight years we have fortunately been without this.
translations.idiomatic: For seven or eight years we have been spared that.

sentences.zh: 若使臣等處置乖方，吝小費而虧大信，使一旦肆行侵掠，則前日之憂立見，何隱之有哉？

translations.literal: If we ministers mishandle affairs, begrudge small costs and break great faith, and they one day raid at will, yesterday's worries will appear at once—what hidden peril would there be?
translations.idiomatic: Mishandle affairs, begrudge small costs, break great faith—and let them raid at will—and yesterday's dread returns at once. What is hidden about that?

sentences.zh: 其所不可知者，俺答老矣，誠恐數年之後，此人既死，諸部無所統一，其中狡黠，互相爭構，假托異辭，遂行侵擾。

translations.literal: What cannot be known is that Altan Khan is old; I truly fear that in a few years, when this man is dead, the tribes will lack a single ruler, the cunning among them will contend and intrigue under false pretexts, and raids will follow.
translations.idiomatic: What cannot be known is that Altan is old. When he dies, the tribes may lack a single lord; the cunning will quarrel under false pretexts and raid again.

sentences.zh: 此則時變之或然，而不可預料者。

translations.literal: This is a contingency of changing times, not something that can be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: That is a contingency of changing times, not something foreseen today.

sentences.zh: 在我處之，亦惟罷貢絕市，閉關固壘以待。

translations.literal: On our side the handling is likewise only to end tribute, cut off markets, close the passes, and strengthen ramparts in waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Our answer then is to end tribute, cut markets, close passes, and strengthen ramparts.

sentences.zh: 仍禁邊將毋得輕舉，使曲常在彼，而直常在我。

translations.literal: Still forbid frontier generals from rash action, so that wrong is always on their side and right always on ours.
translations.idiomatic: Forbid frontier generals rash action, so wrong stays with them and right with us.

sentences.zh: 因機處置，顧後人方略何如耳。

translations.literal: Dispose according to circumstance; let later men's stratagems be what they may.
translations.idiomatic: Dispose as circumstance demands; let later men judge the stratagem.

sentences.zh: 夫封疆之事，無定形亦無定機，惟朝廷任用得人，處置適宜，何必拘拘焉貢市非而戰守是哉？

translations.literal: Frontier affairs have no fixed form and no fixed moment; only if the court employs the right men and disposes fitly—why must one rigidly deem tribute and markets wrong and war and defense right?
translations.idiomatic: Frontier affairs have no fixed form or moment. Employ the right men and act fitly—why bind ourselves to saying tribute and markets are wrong and war and defense right?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，禦戎無上策。

translations.literal: I have also heard that in guarding against barbarians there is no supreme stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that guarding against barbarians admits no supreme stratagem.

sentences.zh: 征戰禍也，和親辱也，賂遺恥心。

translations.literal: War brings calamity; marriage alliances bring shame; gifts bring pain to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: War is calamity, marriage alliance shame, gifts a wound to the heart.

sentences.zh: 今曰貢，則非和親矣；

translations.literal: Today we say tribute—then it is not marriage alliance;
translations.idiomatic: Today we say tribute—not marriage alliance;

sentences.zh: 曰市，則非賂遺矣；

translations.literal: we say markets—then it is not gifts;
translations.idiomatic: we say markets—not gifts;

sentences.zh: 既貢且市，則無征戰矣。

translations.literal: both tribute and markets—then there is no war.
translations.idiomatic: both tribute and markets—and no war.

sentences.zh: 臣幸藉威靈，制伏強梗，得免斧鉞之誅。

translations.literal: I have fortunately relied on imperial majesty to subdue the stubborn and escape execution by axe.
translations.idiomatic: By your majesty's grace I subdued the stubborn and escaped the axe.

sentences.zh: 今受命還朝，不復與聞閫外之事，誠恐議者謂貢市非計，輒有敷陳，國是搖惑。

translations.literal: Now, receiving orders to return to court, I will no longer hear of affairs outside the command, yet I truly fear that debaters will say tribute and markets are no policy and offer arguments that shake the national course.
translations.idiomatic: Now I return to court and will no longer hear frontier affairs, yet I fear debaters will call tribute and markets folly and shake the national course.

sentences.zh: 內則邊臣畏縮，外則部落攜貳，事機乖迕，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Within, frontier officers will shrink in fear; without, tribes will grow divided in loyalty; the moment will go awry, and regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Within, frontier officers will shrink; without, tribes will waver; affairs will go awry beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 臣雖得去，而犬馬之心實有不能一日忘者，謹列上五事。

translations.literal: Though I may leave, the heart of a loyal hound cannot forget for a single day; I respectfully set forth five matters.
translations.idiomatic: Though I depart, a loyal servant's heart cannot forget for a day. I respectfully submit five matters.

sentences.zh: 至京，復奏上款貢圖。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital he again submitted a diagram of submission and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he submitted again a diagram of submission and tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋代崇古為尚書，署吏部事，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Chonggu as minister, acted in the Ministry of Personnel, and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Wang Chonggu as minister, acted for the Ministry of Personnel, and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以平兩廣功，進少保。

translations.literal: For pacifying the two Guang he was advanced to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying the two Guang he was made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 累疏致仕歸，禦書「盡忠」字賜之。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly to retire and return home; the Emperor wrote the character "Utmost Loyalty" and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly to retire; the Emperor bestowed the brush characters "Utmost Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 二十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four he died.

sentences.zh: 逢時才略明練。

translations.literal: Fang Fengshi's talent was bright and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fengshi was brilliant and seasoned in counsel.

sentences.zh: 處置邊事，皆協機宜。

translations.literal: In handling border affairs, all were coordinated to fit the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: In border affairs he always acted in accord with circumstances.

sentences.zh: 其功名與崇古相亞，稱「方、王」雲。

translations.literal: His achievements ranked second only to Wang Chonggu's; they were called "Fang and Wang."
translations.idiomatic: His reputation nearly matched Wang Chonggu's, and the two were spoken of together as "Fang and Wang."

sentences.zh: 吳兌，字君澤，紹興山陰人。

translations.literal: Wu Dui, style Junze, was a native of Shanyin in Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dui, courtesy name Junze, was a native of Shanyin in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign (1559).

sentences.zh: 授兵部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，由郎中遷湖廣參議。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, from bureau director he was transferred to administration vice commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Longqing (1569), he was promoted from bureau director to administration vice commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 調河南，遷薊州兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan, then promoted to vice commissioner for military preparations at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Henan, then promoted to vice commissioner for military preparations at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，擢右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year (1571) he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 兌舉鄉試出高拱門。

translations.literal: Dui had taken the provincial examination as a disciple of Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Dui had passed the provincial examination as a protégé of Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 拱之初罷相也，兌獨送至潞河。

translations.literal: When Gong was first dismissed from the chancellorship, Dui alone escorted him as far as the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao was first removed from the chancellorship, Dui alone accompanied him to the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 及拱再起兼吏部，遂超擢之。

translations.literal: When Gong was restored and also took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, he thereupon promoted Dui above the usual course.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao returned to power and also headed the Ministry of Personnel, he promptly promoted Dui far ahead of the normal schedule.

sentences.zh: 釋褐十三年得節鉞，前此未有也。

translations.literal: Thirteen years after leaving the green he received a military command—a thing unprecedented before.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years after entering official life he received a frontier command with full military authority, something without precedent.

sentences.zh: 時俺答初封貢，而昆都力、辛愛陰持兩端，助其主土蠻為患。

translations.literal: At that time Altan had just been granted tribute and trade, while Kundulun and Singe secretly kept two faces and aided their lord Tümen in making trouble.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Altan had only just been granted tribute and border trade, while Kundulun and Singe secretly played both sides and helped their lord Tümen harass the frontier.

sentences.zh: 兌事智計，操縱馴伏之。

translations.literal: Dui relied on stratagem and manipulated them into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Dui relied on stratagem and skillfully brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 嘗偵俺答離營獵，從五騎直趨其營。

translations.literal: Once, learning that Altan had left camp to hunt, he went with five horsemen straight to the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Once, learning that Altan had left camp to hunt, he rode with only five men straight to the Mongol camp.

sentences.zh: 守者愕，控弦。

translations.literal: The guards were astonished and drew their bows.
translations.idiomatic: The guards were astonished and strung their bows.

sentences.zh: 從騎呵之曰：「太師來犒軍耳！」

translations.literal: His attendants shouted at them, saying, "The Grand Preceptor has come to reward the troops!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants shouted, "The Grand Preceptor has come to reward the troops!

sentences.zh: 皆拜跪迎導，且獻酪。

translations.literal: All bowed and knelt to welcome and guide him, and moreover presented kumiss.
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed and knelt to receive him, presented kumiss, and escorted him about.

sentences.zh: 兌遍閱廬帳，抵暮還。

translations.literal: Dui inspected every tent in turn and returned at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Dui inspected every tent in the camp and returned at dusk.

sentences.zh: 市者或潛盜所鬻馬，兌使人棓擊之，曰：「後復盜，即閉關停市。」

translations.literal: Some in the market secretly stole horses that were being sold; Dui had them beaten with clubs and said, "If there is theft again, the passes will be closed and trade halted."
translations.idiomatic: When market-goers secretly stole horses offered for sale, Dui had them clubbed and announced, "Steal again and we will close the passes and halt the market.

sentences.zh: 諸部追究所奪馬，並執其人以謝。

translations.literal: The tribes tracked down the stolen horses and also seized the thieves to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then recovered the stolen horses and handed over the thieves to make amends.

sentences.zh: 辛愛復擾邊，俺答曰「宣、大，我市場也。」

translations.literal: Singe again harassed the border; Altan said, "Xuan and Da are my marketplaces."
translations.idiomatic: When Singe again raided the frontier, Altan said, "Xuanfu and Datong are my marketplaces.

sentences.zh: 戒勿動。

translations.literal: He forbade any move against them.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade Singe to stir trouble there.

sentences.zh: 然辛愛猶傑驁，俺答常以己馬代入貢。

translations.literal: Yet Singe remained fierce and overbearing; Altan often substituted his own horses when Singe presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Singe remained proud and unruly, and Altan often sent his own horses in Singe's name when tribute was presented.

sentences.zh: 既得賞賜，抵地不肯受，又遣兵掠車夷。

translations.literal: Once the rewards were received, they would not accept them on the ground and again sent troops to plunder the Cheyi.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rewards were issued, Singe would refuse them on the spot and again send troops to plunder the Cheyi.

sentences.zh: 車夷者，不知其所出，自嘉靖中徙至，與史夷雜居，皆宣鎮保塞屬也。

translations.literal: The Cheyi—no one knows whence they came—moved in during the Jiajing period and lived mixed with the Shiyi; both were dependents under Xuanfu's frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheyi, whose origin is unknown, had migrated in during the Jiajing era and lived intermingled with the Shiyi; both groups were subjects under Xuanfu's frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 辛愛掠之，以其長革固去，其二比妓來駐龍門教場。

translations.literal: Singe plundered them and carried off their chief Gegu; his two subsidiary wives came to encamp at the Longmen drill ground.
translations.idiomatic: Singe raided them, carried off their chief Gegu, and two of his subsidiary wives came to camp at the Longmen drill ground.

sentences.zh: 兌以史、車唇齒，車被掠，史益孤，奏築堡居之。

translations.literal: Dui, considering the Shiyi and Cheyi interdependent, and that with the Cheyi plundered the Shiyi would be all the more isolated, memorialized to build a fort for them to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Dui reasoned that the Shiyi and Cheyi stood or fell together; with the Cheyi raided the Shiyi would be isolated. He memorialized to build a fort where they could settle.

sentences.zh: 使使詰責辛愛，令還革固而勒其比妓遠邊。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to rebuke Singe, ordering him to return Gegu and compel the subsidiary wives to withdraw far from the border.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to rebuke Singe, demanding the return of Gegu and that the subsidiary wives withdraw far from the border.

sentences.zh: 辛愛誘比妓五蘭且沁、威兀慎，歲盜葛峪堡器甲、牛羊。

translations.literal: Singe enticed the subsidiary wives, Wulanqien, and Weiwushen, who year after year stole armor, cattle, and sheep from Geyu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Singe drew in the subsidiary wives together with Wulanqien and Weiwushen, who each year stole armor, cattle, and sheep from Geyu Fort.

sentences.zh: 兌皆付三娘子罰治。

translations.literal: Dui handed all of them over to the Third Lady for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Dui turned them all over to the Third Lady for punishment.

sentences.zh: 三娘子有盛寵於俺答，辛愛嫉妒，數詛詈之。

translations.literal: The Third Lady enjoyed great favor with Altan; Singe was jealous and repeatedly cursed and reviled her.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Lady enjoyed great favor with Altan; Singe envied her and repeatedly cursed and abused her.

sentences.zh: 三娘子入貢，宿兌軍中，訴其事。

translations.literal: When the Third Lady came to present tribute she lodged in Dui's camp and told him of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Third Lady came to present tribute she stayed in Dui's camp and told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 兌贈以八寶冠、百鳳雲衣、紅骨朵雲裙，三娘子以此為兌盡力。

translations.literal: Dui gave her a crown of eight treasures, a robe of a hundred phoenixes amid clouds, and a cloud skirt with red bone ornaments; because of this the Third Lady served Dui with all her strength.
translations.idiomatic: Dui presented her with a crown of eight treasures, a robe embroidered with a hundred cloud-phoenixes, and a red cloud skirt with bone ornaments; from then on the Third Lady exerted herself fully on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 辛愛、撦力克相繼襲王，皆妻三娘子，三娘子主貢市者三世。

translations.literal: Singe and Chalük succeeded one another as khans, each marrying the Third Lady; for three generations she controlled tribute and trade.
translations.idiomatic: Singe and Chalük succeeded one another as khans, each taking the Third Lady as wife; for three generations she directed tribute and trade.

sentences.zh: 昆都力嘗求封王，會病死，其子青把都擁兵至塞，多所要挾。

translations.literal: Kundulun once sought investiture as khan; he happened to die of illness, and his son Qingbadu led troops to the frontier with many demands.
translations.idiomatic: Kundulun had once sought investiture as khan; he died of illness, and his son Qingbadu brought troops to the border with numerous demands.

sentences.zh: 兌諭以禍福，而耀武震之。

translations.literal: Dui instructed him in gain and loss, and at the same time awed him with a display of force.
translations.idiomatic: Dui lectured him on advantage and peril while displaying military might to overawe him.

sentences.zh: 青把都懼，貢如初，其女東桂嫁朵顏都督長昂，嘗隨父入貢，訴其貧。

translations.literal: Qingbadu was afraid and presented tribute as before; his daughter Donggui married Chang Ang, commander of the Tümed, and once accompanied her father to tribute, complaining of her poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbadu, afraid, resumed tribute as before. His daughter Donggui married Chang Ang, commander of the Tümed, and once came with her father to present tribute and pleaded her poverty.

sentences.zh: 兌諭其昆弟，每一馬分一繒畀之。

translations.literal: Dui instructed her brothers that for each horse they should give her one bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Dui told her brothers to give her one bolt of silk for each horse presented.

sentences.zh: 後東桂報土蠻別騎掠三岔河東，兌得為備，有功。

translations.literal: Later Donggui reported that Tümen had sent a separate detachment to plunder east of the Sancha River; Dui was able to prepare defenses and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Donggui warned that Tümen had sent a separate force to raid east of the Sancha River; Dui was able to ready defenses and earned merit.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年春，推款貢功，加兌右副都御史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Wanli, on the strength of arranging tribute and trade he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Wanli (1574), for his work in arranging tribute and trade, he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 貢市畢，加兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史。

translations.literal: When tribute and trade were completed, he was further made vice minister of war and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribute season ended, he was further appointed vice minister of war and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，代方逢時總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he replaced Fang Fengshi as supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year (1577) he replaced Fang Fengshi as supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 俺答西掠瓦剌，聲言迎佛，寄帑於兌，留旗箭為信。

translations.literal: Altan raided west into the Oirats, claiming he was going to welcome the Buddha, and deposited goods with Dui, leaving banner arrows as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Altan raided west into the Oirats, claiming he was going to welcome the Buddha. He left goods in Dui's custody and banner arrows as tokens.

sentences.zh: 尚書王崇古奏上方略，使兌諭俺答繞賀蘭山後行，勿道甘肅；

translations.literal: Minister Wang Chonggu memorialized a plan to the throne, having Dui instruct Altan to march behind the Helan range and not pass through Gansu;
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Chonggu submitted a plan to the throne, directing Dui to tell Altan to march behind the Helan Mountains and not pass through Gansu;

sentences.zh: 又陰泄其謀於瓦剌。

translations.literal: he also secretly leaked the plan to the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: he also secretly disclosed the plan to the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 俺答兵遂挫，留青海未歸。

translations.literal: Altan's army was thereupon checked, and he remained in Qinghai without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Altan's army was thereupon checked, and he lingered in Qinghai without returning.

sentences.zh: 而青把都復附土蠻，其部下時入寇。

translations.literal: Qingbadu again attached himself to Tümen, and his subordinates periodically crossed the border to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Qingbadu again joined Tümen, and his followers periodically crossed in to raid.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正令兌趣俺答東還約束之，青把都亦罰治其下，款貢乃益堅。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng ordered Dui to urge Altan to return east and restrain him; Qingbadu also punished his men, and peace-through-tribute grew all the firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng ordered Dui to press Altan to return east and restrain him; Qingbadu also punished his subordinates, and the peace-through-tribute system grew firmer still.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，以左侍郎召還部，尋加右都御史，仍佐部事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he was summoned back to the ministry as left vice minister, and soon added right censor-in-chief while still assisting in ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year (1579) he was recalled to the ministry as left vice minister, soon given the concurrent rank of right censor-in-chief while continuing to assist in ministry business.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，復以本官總督薊、遼、保定軍務兼巡撫順天。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year he again took his former post as supreme commander of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding, concurrently grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the ninth year (1581) he again served as supreme commander of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding, concurrently grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 泰寧速把亥與青把都交通，陰入市宣府，而歲犯遼東以要款。

translations.literal: Subahai of the Taining and Qingbadu were in contact, secretly entering Xuanfu to trade while each year raiding Liaodong to press for peace terms.
translations.idiomatic: Subahai of the Taining and Qingbadu were in league, secretly trading in Xuanfu while raiding Liaodong each year to force favorable terms.

sentences.zh: 朝廷拒不許，兌修義州城備之。

translations.literal: The court refused permission; Dui repaired Yizhou city to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused; Dui repaired Yizhou city to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 明年春，速把亥來寇，總兵官李成梁擊斬之。

translations.literal: The next spring Subahai came to raid; the regional commander Li Chengliang attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Subahai raided; regional commander Li Chengliang attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其弟炒花、侄老撒卜兒悉遁去。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chaohua and his nephew Laosabuer all fled.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chaohua and his nephew Laosabuer all fled.

sentences.zh: 詔進兌兵部尚書仍兼右都御史。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Dui to minister of war while he still held the concurrent rank of right censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Dui to minister of war while he retained the concurrent rank of right censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 尋進太子少保，召拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to junior guardian of the heir apparent and summoned to serve as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made junior guardian of the heir apparent and appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 御史魏允貞劾兌歷附高拱、張居正，且饋馮保金千兩，封識具存。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Yunzhen impeached Dui for having long attached himself to Gao Gong and Zhang Juzheng, and moreover for presenting Feng Bao with a thousand taels of gold, the sealed label still intact.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Yunzhen impeached Dui for long currying favor with Gao Gong and Zhang Juzheng, and for giving the eunuch Feng Bao a thousand taels of gold with the seal still unbroken.

sentences.zh: 給事王繼光亦言兌受將吏饋遺，御史林休徵助之攻。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Jiguang also said Dui accepted gifts from generals and officers; censor Lin Xiuzheng joined in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Jiguang also charged that Dui accepted gifts from generals and officers; censor Lin Xiuzheng joined the attack.

sentences.zh: 帝乃允兌去，後數年卒。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon allowed Dui to leave office; he died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor allowed Dui to retire; he died several years later.

sentences.zh: 孫孟明，襲錦衣千戶，佐許顯純理北司刑。

translations.literal: His grandson Mengming inherited the post of commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard at the thousand-man level and assisted Xu Xianchun in handling cases in the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Mengming inherited a command in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard at the thousand-man level and assisted Xu Xianchun in trials at the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，讞中書汪文言，頗為之左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, in trying the Secretariat clerk Wang Wenyan, he quite often swayed matters in Wang's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign, while trying the Secretariat clerk Wang Wenyan, he often leaned the case Wang's way.

sentences.zh: 顯純怒，誣孟明藏匿亡命。

translations.literal: Xianchun was angry and falsely charged Mengming with harboring fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Xianchun, enraged, falsely charged Mengming with harboring fugitives.

sentences.zh: 下本司拷訊，削籍歸。

translations.literal: He was handed to the prison of his own office for interrogation under torture and was struck from the rolls and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed to his own prison for torture, struck from the rolls, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起故官，累遷都督同知，掌衛事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was restored to his former post, and eventually was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief and directed guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was restored to office, rose eventually to vice commissioner-in-chief, and directed guard affairs.

sentences.zh: 孟明居官貪，以附東林，頗得時譽。

translations.literal: Mengming was corrupt in office; because he sided with the Donglin faction he won considerable contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Mengming was corrupt in office, yet by siding with the Donglin faction he won considerable contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 子邦輔襲職，亦理北司刑。

translations.literal: His son Bangfu inherited the post and also handled cases in the northern prison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bangfu inherited the post and likewise handled cases in the northern prison.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，給事中姜采、行人司副熊開元以言事同日系詔獄，帝欲置之死，邦輔故緩其獄。

translations.literal: Late in Chongzhen, supervising secretary Jiang Cai and vice director of the Pedestrian Office Xiong Kaiyuan were imprisoned on the same day for remonstrance; the emperor wished to put them to death, but Bangfu deliberately slowed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Chongzhen, supervising secretary Jiang Cai and vice director of the Pedestrian Office Xiong Kaiyuan were imprisoned the same day for remonstrance; the emperor wished to execute them, but Bangfu deliberately drew out the trial.

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍解，令嚴訊主使者。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger somewhat eased, and he ordered a strict inquiry into who was behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, and he ordered a strict inquiry into who was behind them.

sentences.zh: 邦輔乃略訊即具獄上，詔予杖百，二人由是獲免。

translations.literal: Bangfu then conducted only a cursory inquiry and at once submitted a completed case; an edict ordered them beaten a hundred times, and the two thereby escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Bangfu then conducted only a perfunctory inquiry and at once submitted a completed dossier. An edict ordered them beaten a hundred strokes, and the two thereby escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 鄭洛，字禹秀，安肅人。

translations.literal: Zheng Luo, style Yuxiu, was a native of Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luo, courtesy name Yuxiu, was a native of Ansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing (1556).

sentences.zh: 除登州推官，征授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed pushi of Dengzhou and, on imperial summons, made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial assistant of Dengzhou and, on imperial summons, made a censor.

sentences.zh: 劾罷嚴嵩黨鄢懋卿、萬寀、萬虞龍。

translations.literal: He impeached and had dismissed Yan Maoqing, Wan Cai, and Wan Yulong, partisans of Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and secured the dismissal of Yan Maoqing, Wan Cai, and Wan Yulong, partisans of Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 出為四川參議，遷山西參政。

translations.literal: He went out as administration commissioner in Sichuan and was transferred to Shanxi as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administration commissioner in Sichuan, then was transferred to the same post in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 佐總督王崇古款俺答有功。

translations.literal: Assisting supreme commander Wang Chonggu in arranging peace with Altan, he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting supreme commander Wang Chonggu in arranging peace with Altan, he earned merit.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，由浙江左布政使改右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, from left administration commissioner of Zhejiang he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli (1574), from left administration commissioner of Zhejiang he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 移大同，加右副都御史，入為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Datong, promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, and entered the ministry as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Datong, promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, and entered the ministry as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 七年，以左侍郎總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as left vice minister he became supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1579), as left vice minister he became supreme commander of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 昆都力子滿五大令銀定入犯，洛奏停貢市，遣使責俺答罰贖駝馬牛羊，乃復許款。

translations.literal: Mandudaling, son of Kundulun, led Yinding in an incursion; Luo memorialized to halt tribute and trade, sent envoys to demand that Altan punish and redeem the camels, horses, cattle, and sheep, and only then permitted peace again.
translations.idiomatic: Mandudaling, son of Kundulun, led Yinding in a raid. Luo memorialized to suspend tribute and trade, sent envoys to demand that Altan punish the offenders and redeem the camels, horses, cattle, and sheep, and only then allowed peace to resume.

sentences.zh: 三娘子佐俺答主貢市，諸部皆受其約束。

translations.literal: The Third Lady assisted Altan in directing tribute and trade, and all the tribes were subject to her restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Lady assisted Altan in managing tribute and trade, and all the tribes were bound by her authority.

sentences.zh: 及辛愛襲封，年老且病，欲妻三娘子。

translations.literal: When Singe succeeded to the title, old and ill, he wished to take the Third Lady as wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Singe succeeded to the title, old and ill, he wished to take the Third Lady as wife.

sentences.zh: 三娘子不從，率眾西走，辛愛自追之，貢市久不至。

translations.literal: The Third Lady would not consent and led her followers west; Singe pursued her himself, and tribute and trade long failed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Lady refused and led her followers west; Singe pursued her in person, and tribute and trade long ceased.

sentences.zh: 洛計三娘子別屬，則辛愛雖王無益，乃使人語之曰：「夫人能歸王，不失恩寵，否則塞上一婦人耳。」

translations.literal: Luo reasoned that if the Third Lady belonged to another, Singe would be khan in name only without benefit, and sent someone to tell her, saying, "If the lady returns to the khan, you will not lose favor; otherwise you are but a woman on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Luo reasoned that if the Third Lady attached herself elsewhere, Singe would be khan in name only. He sent word to her: "If you return to the khan, you will not lose favor; otherwise you are but another woman on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 三娘子聽命。

translations.literal: The Third Lady obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Lady obeyed.

sentences.zh: 辛愛更名乞慶哈，貢市惟謹。

translations.literal: Singe changed his name to Qiqingha, and tribute and trade were thereafter scrupulously observed.
translations.idiomatic: Singe took the name Qiqingha, and tribute and trade were thereafter conducted with care.

sentences.zh: 洛以功加兵部尚書兼右副都御史。

translations.literal: Luo, for his merit, was promoted to minister of war and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Luo was promoted to minister of war and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，乞慶哈死，子撦力克當襲。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Qiqingha died, and his son Chalük was to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1586) Qiqingha died, and his son Chalük was to succeed.

sentences.zh: 三娘子以年長，自練兵萬人，築城別居。

translations.literal: The Third Lady, by reason of her seniority, herself drilled ten thousand troops and built a separate walled residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Third Lady, by reason of her seniority, herself drilled ten thousand troops and built a separate walled residence.

sentences.zh: 洛恐貢市無主，復諭撦力克曰：「夫人三世歸順，汝能與之匹，則王，不然封別有屬也。」

translations.literal: Luo feared that tribute and trade would lack a head; he again instructed Chalük, saying, "The lady has been loyal for three generations; if you can match her, you shall be khan—otherwise investiture will go elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Luo feared tribute and trade would lack a head. He again told Chalük, "The lady has been loyal for three generations; if you can stand as her equal you shall be khan—otherwise the title will go elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 撦力克盡逐諸妾，復妻三娘子。

translations.literal: Chalük drove out all his other wives and again took the Third Lady as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chalük drove out all his other wives and again took the Third Lady as wife.

sentences.zh: 遂以明年嗣封，並奏封三娘子忠順夫人。

translations.literal: He thereupon succeeded to the title the next year, and together they memorialized to enfeoff the Third Lady as Lady Zhongshun.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded the next year and jointly memorialized to enfeoff the Third Lady as Lady Zhongshun.

sentences.zh: 洛乃上疏請定市馬數，宣府不得逾三萬，大同萬四千，山西六千，而申飭將吏嚴備，以防盜竊，且無輕遏其部落馳獵者。

translations.literal: Luo then memorialized to fix the number of horses for border trade—no more than thirty thousand for Xuanfu, fourteen thousand for Datong, six thousand for Shanxi—and to admonish generals and officers to stand firm guard against theft, and not lightly to obstruct the tribes when hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo then memorialized to fix horse quotas for border trade—no more than thirty thousand at Xuanfu, fourteen thousand at Datong, six thousand in Shanxi—and to warn generals and officers to guard strictly against theft and not lightly obstruct tribal hunting.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 御史許守恩劾洛。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Shou'en impeached Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Shou'en impeached Luo.

sentences.zh: 乞歸，不允。

translations.literal: He begged to retire and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and was refused.

sentences.zh: 自太子少保累加至太子太保，召為戎政尚書。

translations.literal: From junior guardian of the heir apparent he was repeatedly promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent and summoned as minister of military administration.
translations.idiomatic: From junior guardian of the heir apparent he rose step by step to grand guardian and was summoned as minister of military administration.

sentences.zh: 十八年，洮河用兵，詔兼右都御史，經略陜西、延、寧、甘肅及宣、大、山西邊務。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, with war on the Tao River, an edict made him concurrently right censor-in-chief to oversee Shaanxi, Yan, Ning, Gansu, and the frontier affairs of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1590), with war on the Tao River, an edict made him concurrently right censor-in-chief to oversee Shaanxi, Yan, Ning, Gansu, and the frontiers of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 松套賓兔等屢越甘肅侵擾河、湟諸番。

translations.literal: Guests such as Bintu of Songtao repeatedly crossed Gansu to harass the Fan along the Huang and Tao rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders such as Bintu of Songtao repeatedly crossed Gansu to harass the Tibetan peoples along the Huang and Tao rivers.

sentences.zh: 及俺答迎佛，又建寺於青海，奏賜名仰華，留永邵卜別部把爾戶及丙兔、火落赤守之，俱牧海上。

translations.literal: When Altan went to welcome the Buddha he also built a temple at Qinghai; the court granted the name Yanghua, leaving Barhu of Yongshaobu's separate division and Bingtu and Huolochi to guard it, all pasturing on the sea of grass.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan went to welcome the Buddha he also built a temple at Qinghai; the court granted the name Yanghua and left Barhu of Yongshaobu's separate division together with Bingtu and Huolochi to guard it, all pasturing on the Qinghai grasslands.

sentences.zh: 他部往來者，率取道甘肅，甘肅鎮臣以通款弗禁也。

translations.literal: Other tribes passing through generally took the Gansu route; the Gansu commander, because peace had been granted, did not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Other tribes traveling through generally took the Gansu route; the Gansu commander, because peace had been granted, did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 丙兔死，其子真相進據莽剌川，火落赤據捏工川，益並吞番族。

translations.literal: When Bingtu died, his son Zhenxiang advanced and seized Mangchuan; Huolochi seized Niegongchuan, swallowing Fan territory all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingtu died, his son Zhenxiang advanced and seized Mangchuan; Huolochi seized Niegongchuan, further swallowing Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 河套都督卜失兔亦遣使邀撦力克，撦力克遺洛書，以赴仰華為名。

translations.literal: Bushitu, commander of the Ordos, also sent envoys to invite Chalük; Chalük sent Luo a letter, on the pretext of going to Yanghua.
translations.idiomatic: Bushitu, commander of the Ordos, also sent envoys to invite Chalük; Chalük wrote to Luo, claiming he was going to Yanghua.

sentences.zh: 洛使從塞外行，又諭忠順夫人曰：「彼中撫賞不能多，且王家在東，恐有內顧憂也。」

translations.literal: Luo had him go by the route outside the passes and also told Lady Zhongshun, saying, "Rewards on that side cannot be large, and with your house in the east you may fear looking homeward."
translations.idiomatic: Luo had him march outside the passes and also told Lady Zhongshun, "Rewards in the west cannot be generous, and with your house in the east you may worry about turning back.

sentences.zh: 撦力克遂行。

translations.literal: Chalük then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Chalük then set out.

sentences.zh: 未至，把爾戶部卒闌入西寧。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, soldiers of Barhu's division burst into Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, troops of Barhu's division broke into Xining.

sentences.zh: 副總兵李奎方醉，單騎馳之。

translations.literal: Vice commander Li Kui was drunk and rode out alone.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commander Li Kui, drunk, rode out alone.

sentences.zh: 卒持鞚自白，為奎所斫，遂大噪，射奎死。

translations.literal: A soldier held the bridle to explain himself and was cut down by Kui; thereupon they raised a great clamor, shot Kui, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier seized his bridle to explain; Kui struck him down. They thereupon raised a great uproar, shot Kui, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 火落赤、真相進圍舊洮州，副總兵李聯芳敗歿。

translations.literal: Huolochi and Zhenxiang advanced and besieged Old Taozhou; vice commander Li Lianfang was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huolochi and Zhenxiang advanced and besieged Old Taozhou; vice commander Li Lianfang was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 入臨洮、河州、渭源，總兵官劉承嗣失利，遊擊李芳等皆死。

translations.literal: They entered Lintao, Hezhou, and Weiyuan; regional commander Liu Chengsi was defeated, and guerrilla commander Li Fang and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: They entered Lintao, Hezhou, and Weiyuan; regional commander Liu Chengsi was defeated, and guerrilla commander Li Fang and others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 當是時，撦力克已至仰華，火落赤、真相益挾為重，關中大震，惟把爾戶不助逆。

translations.literal: At that time Chalük had already reached Yanghua; Huolochi and Zhenxiang relied on him all the more, Guanzhong was greatly shaken, and only Barhu did not aid the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chalük had reached Yanghua; Huolochi and Zhenxiang leaned on him all the more. Guanzhong was shaken, and only Barhu did not join the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔洛經略七鎮，以僉事萬世德、兵部員外郎梁雲龍隨軍贊畫，而停撦力克貢市。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, an edict put Luo in charge of seven commands, with commissioner Wan Shide and ministry bureau director Liang Yunlong to assist in planning, and halted Chalük's tribute and trade.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict put Luo in charge of seven commands, with commissioner Wan Shide and ministry bureau director Liang Yunlong to assist in planning, and suspended Chalük's tribute and trade.

sentences.zh: 俄罷總督梅友松，命洛兼領其事。

translations.literal: Soon supreme commander Mei Yousong was dismissed and Luo was ordered to take over that duty as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon supreme commander Mei Yousong was dismissed and Luo was ordered to assume that post as well.

sentences.zh: 洛以洮河之禍，由縱敵入青海，乃馳至甘肅，令曰：「北部自青海歸巢者，聽假道；

translations.literal: Luo held that the Tao River disaster came from allowing the enemy into Qinghai, and hastened to Gansu with an order: "Northerners returning from Qinghai to their nests may be allowed passage;
translations.idiomatic: Luo held that the Tao River disaster came from letting the enemy into Qinghai. He hastened to Gansu and proclaimed, "Northerners returning from Qinghai to their home pastures may pass through;

sentences.zh: 自巢入青海者，即勒兵拒之。」

translations.literal: those going from their nests into Qinghai are to be met with troops and barred."
translations.idiomatic: those going from their pastures into Qinghai are to be met with troops and turned back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卜失兔至水泉，欲趨青海。

translations.literal: Before long Bushitu reached Shuiquan and wished to hurry to Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bushitu reached Shuiquan and wished to press on to Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 總兵官張臣與相持月余，洛設伏掩擊之，卜失兔僅以身免。

translations.literal: Regional commander Zhang Chen faced him in stalemate for more than a month; Luo set an ambush and struck him; Bushitu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Zhang Chen faced him in stalemate for more than a month; Luo set an ambush and struck; Bushitu barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 莊禿賴後至，聞之亦退去。

translations.literal: Zhuangtulai arrived later; hearing of it, he too withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtulai arrived later; hearing of it, he too withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，洛與雲龍入西寧，控扼青海。

translations.literal: The next year Luo and Yunlong entered Xining and controlled Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Luo and Yunlong entered Xining and secured Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 撦力克聞之，西徙二百里，還洮河所掠人口，與忠順夫人輸罪請歸。

translations.literal: When Chalük heard of it he moved west two hundred li, returned the people plundered on the Tao River, and with Lady Zhongshun submitted guilt and asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Chalük heard of it he moved west two hundred li, returned the people plundered on the Tao River, and with Lady Zhongshun confessed guilt and asked to return.

sentences.zh: 火落赤、真相亦夜去，兩川余黨留莽敕南山。

translations.literal: Huolochi and Zhenxiang also left by night; remnant bands of the two valleys remained on Mangchi South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Huolochi and Zhenxiang also withdrew by night; remnant bands of the two valleys remained on Mangchi South Mountain.

sentences.zh: 洛慮諸部約結，先遣使趣撦力克北歸，別遣雲龍、世德收番族以弱其勢，而具以狀奏聞。

translations.literal: Luo, fearing the tribes would league together, first sent envoys to urge Chalük to return north, separately sent Yunlong and Shide to win over the Fan and weaken their strength, and fully reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, fearing the tribes would league together, first sent envoys to urge Chalük north, separately sent Yunlong and Shide to win over the Tibetans and weaken the enemy, and reported the full situation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 言：「自順義南牧，借途收番，子女牛羊皆有之，生死唯所制。

translations.literal: He said, "Since the Shunyi [khan] pastured south, taking passage to absorb the Fan, they gained wives, children, cattle, and sheep; life and death were at their disposal.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "Since the Shunyi Khan pastured south, using the route to absorb Tibetans, they gained wives, children, cattle, and sheep and held life and death in their hands.

sentences.zh: 洮河之役，遂為向導，番戎之勢不分，則心腹之患無已。

translations.literal: In the Tao River campaign they served as guides; if Fan strength were not divided, the danger to our vitals would never end.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tao River campaign they served as guides. If Tibetan strength were not divided, the peril to our heartland would never end.

sentences.zh: 臣鼓舞勞來，招回諸番八萬余人，皆陛下威德所致。」

translations.literal: I have encouraged and comforted them and brought back more than eighty thousand of the Fan—this is all from Your Majesty's majesty and virtue."
translations.idiomatic: I have encouraged and won back more than eighty thousand Tibetans—all through Your Majesty's majesty and virtue.

sentences.zh: 且具陳收番有六利。

translations.literal: He also set forth in detail six advantages in winning over the Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth in detail six advantages in winning over the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 是時，撦力克觀望不即歸，洛與相羈縻，先遣總兵官尤繼先擊走莽剌余寇。
