translations.literal: At that time Chalük hesitated and did not return at once; Luo held him in check while first sending regional commander You Jixian to drive off the remnant raiders of Mangchi.
translations.idiomatic: Chalük hesitated and did not return at once; Luo kept him in check while first sending regional commander You Jixian to drive off the Mangchi remnant raiders.

sentences.zh: 督撫魏學曾、葉夢熊等請決戰，夢熊又騰書都下，洛疏持不可。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators Wei Xueceng and Ye Mengxiong requested a decisive battle; Mengxiong also sent inflammatory letters to the capital, but Luo memorialized to hold firm against it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators Wei Xueceng and Ye Mengxiong urged a decisive battle; Mengxiong also sent inflammatory letters to the capital, but Luo memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 夢熊乃調苗兵三千為選鋒，詆洛為秦檜、賈似道。

translations.literal: Mengxiong then deployed three thousand Miao troops as an assault corps and slandered Luo as Qin Hui and Jia Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxiong then deployed three thousand Miao troops as shock troops and slandered Luo as Qin Hui and Jia Sidao.

sentences.zh: 會撦力克北歸謝罪，乞復貢市，洛乃進兵青海，走火落赤、真相，焚仰華，置戍西寧、歸德而還。

translations.literal: When Chalük returned north to apologize and begged to resume tribute and trade, Luo advanced into Qinghai, drove off Huolochi and Zhenxiang, burned Yanghua, garrisoned Xining and Guide, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chalük returned north to apologize and begged to resume tribute and trade, Luo advanced into Qinghai, drove off Huolochi and Zhenxiang, burned Yanghua, posted garrisons at Xining and Guide, and returned.

sentences.zh: 尚書石星以宣、大事急，請速召洛究款戰之計。

translations.literal: Minister Shi Xing, because Xuan affairs were urgent, asked that Luo be quickly summoned to settle the plan for peace or war.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shi Xing, because affairs on the Xuan frontier were urgent, asked that Luo be quickly summoned to settle the plan for peace or war.

sentences.zh: 洛既至，與總督蕭大亨、巡撫王世揚、邢玠等上疏曰：「撦力克諉罪火落赤、真相，桀驁之狀已斂。

translations.literal: When Luo arrived, together with supreme commander Xiao Dayheng and grand coordinators Wang Shiyang and Xing Zhi he memorialized, saying, "Chalük blames Huolochi and Zhenxiang; their arrogant conduct has already been curbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo arrived, he joined supreme commander Xiao Dayheng and grand coordinators Wang Shiyang and Xing Zhi in a memorial: "Chalük blames Huolochi and Zhenxiang; their arrogance has already been curbed.

sentences.zh: 且其部落數千里，部長十余輩。

translations.literal: Moreover his tribes extend thousands of li, with more than ten chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His tribes extend thousands of li, with more than ten chiefs.

sentences.zh: 在巢保疆者，宣鎮則青把都兄弟未嘗東窺薊、遼，而兀慎、擺腰五路之在新平，馴服猶故。

translations.literal: Those guarding the frontier in their nests—at Xuanfu Qingbadu and his brothers have not looked east toward Ji and Liaodong, while the Wuzhen and Baiyao five routes at Xinping remain as tame as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those guarding the frontier in their home pastures—at Xuanfu Qingbadu and his brothers have not looked east toward Ji and Liaodong, while the Wuzhen and Baiyao five routes at Xinping remain as tame as before.

sentences.zh: 在西行牧者，不他失未嘗窺莽、捏，而大成比妓則又歸巢獨先。

translations.literal: Those pasturing west—Butashi has not eyed Mang and Nie, while Dacheng's subsidiary wives were the first to return to their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Those pasturing west—Butashi has not eyed Mangchuan and Niegongchuan, while Dacheng's subsidiary wives were the first to return home.

sentences.zh: 今以一人之罪，概絕諸部，消往日之恩，開將來之隙，臣未見其可。

translations.literal: Now for one man's crime to cut off all the tribes, canceling past kindness and opening future rifts—I do not see how that can be done.
translations.idiomatic: To cut off all the tribes for one man's crime, canceling past kindness and opening future rifts—I do not see how that can be justified.

sentences.zh: 今史二外叛，屢犯邊疆，若令順義王縛獻以著信，然後酌議市賞，在我固未為失策也。」

translations.literal: Now the two Shiyi outside have rebelled and repeatedly violated the frontier; if the Shunyi king binds and presents them to show good faith, then we may weigh tribute and rewards—in our view that is not a losing policy."
translations.idiomatic: Now the two outer Shiyi have rebelled and repeatedly raid the frontier. If the Shunyi Khan binds and presents them to show good faith, we may then weigh tribute and rewards—in our view that is no losing policy.

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The decision was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The decision was settled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 尋加少保，仍召理戎政。

translations.literal: Soon he was made junior guardian and again summoned to direct military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made junior guardian and again summoned to direct military administration.

sentences.zh: 順義王果縛史二來獻，復款如故。

translations.literal: The Shunyi king indeed bound the two Shiyi and presented them; peace was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunyi Khan indeed bound the two Shiyi and presented them; peace was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 初，閱邊給事中張棟言，洮河之衄，殞將喪師，洛為其所輕，故東西移帳自便。

translations.literal: Earlier, border-inspecting supervising secretary Zhang Dong had said that the Tao River defeat, with generals killed and troops lost, was lightly regarded by Luo, who therefore shifted camps east and west at his convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, border-inspecting supervising secretary Zhang Dong had said that after the Tao River defeat, with generals killed and troops lost, Luo was treated lightly and therefore shifted camps east and west at his convenience.

sentences.zh: 太仆寺丞徐琰復詆洛，乞處分以除誤國之罪。

translations.literal: Assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xu Yan again slandered Luo, begging that he be punished to remove the crime of harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xu Yan again slandered Luo, asking that he be punished to remove the crime of harming the state.

sentences.zh: 棟再疏劾洛欺罔，給事中章尚學亦請令洛回宣、大。

translations.literal: Dong again memorialized to impeach Luo for deception; supervising secretary Zhang Shangxue also asked that Luo be sent back to Xuan and Da.
translations.idiomatic: Dong again memorialized to impeach Luo for deception; supervising secretary Zhang Shangxue also asked that Luo be sent back to Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 至是撦力克歸，棟又言：「火、真亂首，順義亂階，洛宜除兇雪恥，乃虛詞誘敵，而重利媚之。

translations.literal: When Chalük returned, Dong again said, "Huolochi and Zhenxiang are the leaders of the disorder and the Shunyi khan the stair to disorder; Luo ought to eliminate the villains and wipe away shame, yet he uses empty words to lure the enemy while richly rewarding them with bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Chalük returned, Dong again wrote, "Huolochi and Zhenxiang are the ringleaders and the Shunyi Khan the stepping-stone to disorder. Luo ought to destroy the villains and wipe away shame, yet he uses empty words to lure the enemy while richly bribing them.

sentences.zh: 今火、真依海為窟，出沒如故，洛輒侈然敘文武勞。

translations.literal: Now Huolochi and Zhenxiang rely on the sea as a lair and come and go as before, yet Luo grandly records civil and military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huolochi and Zhenxiang still rely on the sea as a lair and raid as before, yet Luo grandly records civil and military merit.

sentences.zh: 乞敕所司，毋徇洛請。」

translations.literal: I beg that the responsible offices not indulge Luo's requests."
translations.idiomatic: I beg the responsible offices not indulge Luo's requests.

sentences.zh: 洛乃謝病歸。

translations.literal: Luo thereupon pleaded illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Luo thereupon pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 尚書星言洛無重利啖敵事，且有威望，不宜久棄。

translations.literal: Minister Xing said Luo had not richly bribed the enemy and had prestige; he should not long be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xing said Luo had not richly bribed the enemy and had prestige; he should not long be left unused.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，官軍與番人夾擊把爾戶於西寧，大破之。

translations.literal: After more than three years, government troops together with the Fan struck Barhu at Xining and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: More than three years later, government troops together with the Tibetans struck Barhu at Xining and inflicted a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 星復奏洛收番之功，再詔起用。

translations.literal: Xing again memorialized Luo's merit in winning over the Fan, and an edict again ordered his recall.
translations.idiomatic: Xing again memorialized Luo's merit in winning over the Tibetans, and an edict again ordered his recall.

sentences.zh: 當時以洛有物議，卒不推也。

translations.literal: At the time, because Luo was controversial, in the end he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because Luo was controversial, he was in the end not promoted.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made grand guardian and given the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made grand guardian and given the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 張學顏，字子愚，肥鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xueyan, style Ziyu, was a native of Feixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xueyan, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of Feixiang.

sentences.zh: 生九月失母，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: At nine months he lost his mother and served his stepmother with a fame for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at nine months and served his stepmother with a reputation for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 親喪廬墓，有白雀來巢。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parents he built a hut at the tomb; white magpies came to nest.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents he built a mourning hut at the tomb; white magpies came to nest there.

sentences.zh: 登嘉靖三十二年進士，由曲沃知縣入為工科給事中。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing and, from magistrate of Quwo, entered office as a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing (1553) and, from magistrate of Quwo, entered office as a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷山西參議，以總督江東劾去官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administration vice commissioner in Shanxi and was impeached and removed by supreme commander Jiang Dong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to administration vice commissioner in Shanxi and was impeached and removed by supreme commander Jiang Dong.

sentences.zh: 事白，遷永平兵備副使，再調薊州。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared he was made vice commissioner for military preparations at Yongping, then transferred again to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was cleared he was made vice commissioner for military preparations at Yongping, then transferred again to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 俺答封順義王，察罕土門汗語其下曰：「俺答，奴也，而封王，吾顧弗如。」

translations.literal: When Altan was enfeoffed as the Shunyi king, Chahan Tumen Khan said to his followers, "Altan is a slave, yet he is made king—I am not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: When Altan was enfeoffed as Shunyi Khan, Chahan Tumen Khan told his followers, "Altan is a slave, yet he is made king—I am not his equal.

sentences.zh: 挾三衛窺遼，欲以求王。

translations.literal: He took the Three Guards and eyed Liaodong, wishing to obtain a royal title thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Three Guards and eyed Liaodong, seeking a royal title thereby.

sentences.zh: 而海、建諸部日強，皆建國稱汗。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Haixi and Jianzhou tribes grew stronger day by day, each establishing a state and calling themselves khan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Haixi and Jianzhou tribes grew stronger daily, each establishing a state and calling themselves khan.

sentences.zh: 大將王治道、郎得功戰死，遼人大恐。

translations.literal: Generals Wang Zhidao and Lang Degong died in battle, and the people of Liaodong were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wang Zhidao and Lang Degong died in battle, and the people of Liaodong were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年二月，遼撫李秋免，大學士高拱欲用學顏，或疑之，拱曰：「張生卓犖倜儻，人未之識也，置諸盤錯，利器當見。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Longqing the Liaodong grand coordinator Li Qiu was dismissed; Grand Secretary Gao Gong wished to use Xueyan; some doubted it, and Gong said, "Student Zhang is outstanding and bold—people have not yet recognized him; place him amid tangled affairs and the sharp tool will show."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Longqing (1571) Liaodong grand coordinator Li Qiu was dismissed. Grand Secretary Gao Gong wished to appoint Xueyan; some doubted it, and Gao said, "Zhang is outstanding and bold—people have not yet recognized him. Put him amid tangled affairs and the sharp tool will show.

sentences.zh: 侍郎魏學曾後至，拱迎問曰：「遼撫誰可者？」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wei Xueceng arrived later; Gong met him and asked, "Who is fit for Liaodong grand coordinator?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wei Xueceng arrived later; Gao met him and asked, "Who is fit for Liaodong grand coordinator?"

sentences.zh: 學曾思良久，曰：「張學顏可。」

translations.literal: Xueceng thought a long while and said, "Zhang Xueyan will do."
translations.idiomatic: Xueceng thought a long while and said, "Zhang Xueyan will do."

sentences.zh: 拱喜曰：「得之矣。」

translations.literal: Gong said with pleasure, "I have got him."
translations.idiomatic: Gong said with pleasure, "I have got him."

sentences.zh: 遂以其名上，進右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted his name and Xueyan was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the name, and Xueyan was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 遼鎮邊長二千餘里，城砦一百二十所，三面鄰敵。

translations.literal: The Liaodong frontier was more than two thousand li long, with a hundred and twenty walled posts and forts, bordered by enemies on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong frontier stretched more than two thousand li, with a hundred and twenty forts and walled posts, bordered by enemies on three sides.

sentences.zh: 官軍七萬二千，月給米一石，折銀二錢五分，馬則冬春給料，月折銀一錢八分，即歲稔不足支數日。

translations.literal: Official troops numbered seventy-two thousand; each month they were issued a picul of grain, converted to two mace five candareens of silver; horses in winter and spring received fodder, converted to one mace eight candareens a month—even in a good year supplies lasted only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Official troops numbered seventy-two thousand. Each month they received a picul of grain, commuted to two mace five candareens of silver; horses in winter and spring received fodder, commuted to one mace eight candareens monthly—even in a good year supplies lasted only a few days.

sentences.zh: 自嘉靖戊午大饑，士馬逃故者三分之二。

translations.literal: From the great famine of wuwu in Jiajing, two-thirds of men and horses had fled or perished.
translations.idiomatic: From the great famine of the Jiajing wuwu year, two-thirds of men and horses had fled or perished.

sentences.zh: 前撫王之誥、魏學曾相繼綏輯，未復全盛之半。

translations.literal: Former grand coordinators Wang Zhihao and Wei Xueceng in succession had soothed and gathered them, but had not restored even half the former strength.
translations.idiomatic: Former grand coordinators Wang Zhihao and Wei Xueceng had in succession soothed and gathered them, but had not restored even half the former strength.

sentences.zh: 繼以荒旱，餓莩枕籍。

translations.literal: Famine and drought followed, and the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and drought followed, and the dead lay piled one upon another.

sentences.zh: 學顏首請振恤，實軍伍，招流移，治甲仗，市戰馬，信賞罰。

translations.literal: Xueyan first requested relief, filled out the ranks, recalled refugees, readied armor and weapons, purchased war horses, and made rewards and punishments trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan first requested relief, filled the ranks, recalled refugees, readied armor and weapons, purchased war horses, and made rewards and punishments credible.

sentences.zh: 黜懦將數人，創平陽堡以通兩河，移遊擊於正安堡以衛鎮城，戰守具悉就經畫。

translations.literal: He dismissed several cowardly generals, built Pingyang Fort to link the two rivers, moved guerrilla forces to Zheng'an Fort to guard the prefectural city, and fully arranged offensive and defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed several cowardly generals, built Pingyang Fort to link the two rivers, moved guerrilla forces to Zheng'an Fort to guard the prefectural city, and fully arranged offensive and defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 大將李成梁敢力戰深入，而學顏則以收保為完策，敵至無所亡失，敵退備如初，公私力完，漸復其舊。

translations.literal: Great general Li Chengliang dared to fight deep in enemy country, while Xueyan took holding fast and preserving strength as the complete policy; when the enemy came nothing was lost, when the enemy withdrew defenses were as before, public and private strength was restored, and gradually the old order returned.
translations.idiomatic: Great general Li Chengliang dared to fight deep in enemy territory, while Xueyan made holding the defenses and preserving strength his complete policy. When the enemy came nothing was lost; when they withdrew defenses stood as before. Public and private strength was restored, and gradually the old order returned.

sentences.zh: 十一月，與成梁破土蠻卓山，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, together with Chengliang he broke Tümen at Zhuoshan and was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, together with Chengliang he defeated Tümen at Zhuoshan and was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年春，土蠻謀入寇，聞有備而止。

translations.literal: The next spring Tümen plotted to invade but, hearing there were preparations, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Tümen plotted to invade but, hearing defenses were ready, stopped.

sentences.zh: 奸民闌出海上，踞三十六島。

translations.literal: Evil men slipped out to sea and occupied the thirty-six islands.
translations.idiomatic: Evil men slipped out to sea and occupied the thirty-six islands.

sentences.zh: 閱視侍郎汪道昆議緝捕，學顏謂緝捕非便。

translations.literal: Touring inspector Wang Daokun planned to hunt them down; Xueyan said hunting them down was not expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Touring inspector Wang Daokun planned to hunt them down; Xueyan said that was not expedient.

sentences.zh: 命李成梁按兵海上，示將加誅，別遣使招諭，許免差役。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Chengliang to hold troops at sea, showing that punishment would follow, and separately sent envoys to summon and instruct them, promising exemption from corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Chengliang to hold troops at sea as if punishment would follow, and separately sent envoys to summon and instruct them, promising exemption from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 未半載，招還四千四百余口，積患以消。

translations.literal: In less than half a year more than four thousand four hundred persons were brought back, and the long-standing trouble was dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: In less than half a year more than four thousand four hundred persons were brought back, and the long-standing trouble was dispelled.

sentences.zh: 秋，建州都督王杲以索降人不得，入掠撫順，守將賈汝翼詰責之。

translations.literal: In autumn Jianzhou commander Wang Gao, because he did not obtain surrendered people, entered to plunder Fushun; defending officer Jia Ruyi rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Jianzhou commander Wang Gao, failing to obtain surrendered people he demanded, raided Fushun; defending officer Jia Ruyi rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 杲益憾，約諸部為寇，副總兵趙完責汝翼啟釁，學顏奏曰：「汝翼卻杲饋遺，懲其違抗，實伸國威，茍緣此罷斥，是進退邊將皆敵主之矣。

translations.literal: Gao was all the more resentful and agreed with the tribes to raid; vice commander Zhao Wan blamed Ruyi for provoking trouble; Xueyan memorialized, saying, "Ruyi refused Gao's gifts and punished his defiance—it truly extended national majesty; if he is dismissed for this, advancing and retiring frontier generals will all be at the enemy's bidding.
translations.idiomatic: Gao grew more resentful and agreed with the tribes to raid. Vice commander Zhao Wan blamed Ruyi for provoking trouble. Xueyan memorialized, "Ruyi refused Gao's gifts and punished his defiance—it truly extended national majesty. If he is dismissed for this, advancing and retiring frontier generals will all be at the enemy's bidding.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜諭王杲送還俘掠，否則調兵剿殺，毋事姑息以蓄禍。」

translations.literal: I hold that Wang Gao should be instructed to return captives; otherwise troops should be sent to exterminate him—do not indulge him and store up disaster."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Wang Gao should be ordered to return captives; otherwise troops should be sent to exterminate him—do not indulge him and store up disaster.

sentences.zh: 趙完懼，饋金貂，學顏發之，詔逮完，而宣諭王杲如學顏策。

translations.literal: Zhao Wan was afraid and presented gold and sable; Xueyan exposed it; an edict arrested Wan, and Wang Gao was instructed as Xueyan had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wan, afraid, presented gold and sable; Xueyan exposed it. An edict arrested Wan, and Wang Gao was instructed as Xueyan had proposed.

sentences.zh: 諸部聞大兵且出，悉竄匿山谷。

translations.literal: When the tribes heard that great forces were about to march out, they all hid in valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes heard great forces were about to march, they all hid in the valleys.

sentences.zh: 杲懼，十二月約海西王臺送俘獲就款，學顏因而撫之。

translations.literal: Gao was afraid; in the twelfth month he agreed with Haixi king Tai to send captives and come to terms, and Xueyan thereupon pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was afraid; in the twelfth month he agreed with Haixi king Tai to send captives and submit, and Xueyan thereupon pacified him.

sentences.zh: 遼陽鎮東二百餘里舊有孤山堡，巡按御史張鐸增置險山五堡，然與遼鎮聲援不接。

translations.literal: East of Liaoyang town, more than two hundred li away, there had long been Gushan Fort; touring censor Zhang Duo added five forts at Xianshan, yet they did not link in mutual support with the Liaodong command.
translations.idiomatic: East of Liaoyang, more than two hundred li away, there had long been Gushan Fort; touring censor Zhang Duo added five forts at Xianshan, yet they did not link in mutual support with the Liaodong command.

sentences.zh: 都御史王之誥奏設險山參將，轄六堡一十二城，分守叆陽。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wang Zhihao memorialized to establish a vice commander at Xianshan, governing six forts and twelve cities, with divided defense at Aiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wang Zhihao memorialized to establish a vice commander at Xianshan governing six forts and twelve cities, with divided defense at Aiyang.

sentences.zh: 又以其地不毛，欲移置寬佃，以時絀不果。

translations.literal: Also because the land was barren he wished to move the post to Kuandian, but owing to seasonal shortages it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Because the land was barren he also wished to move the post to Kuandian, but seasonal shortages prevented it.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，李成梁議移孤山堡於張其哈佃，移險山五堡於寬佃、長佃、雙墩、長領散等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Li Chengliang proposed moving Gushan Fort to Zhangqiha Tun and the five Xianshan forts to Kuandian, Changdian, Shuangdun, Changling, and San.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wanli, Li Chengliang proposed moving Gushan Fort to Zhangqiha Tun and the five Xianshan forts to Kuandian, Changdian, Shuangdun, Changling, and San.

sentences.zh: 皆據膏腴，扼要害。

translations.literal: All occupied fertile ground and controlled strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: All occupied fertile ground and controlled strategic points.

sentences.zh: 而邊人苦遠役，出怨言。

translations.literal: Yet frontier people complained of distant service and uttered grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Yet frontier people complained of distant service and murmured against it.

sentences.zh: 工甫興，王杲復犯邊，殺遊擊裴承祖。

translations.literal: Work had just begun when Wang Gao again violated the border and killed guerrilla commander Pei Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Work had just begun when Wang Gao again violated the border and killed guerrilla commander Pei Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史亟請罷役，學顏不可，曰：「如此則示弱也。」

translations.literal: The touring censor urgently asked to halt the project; Xueyan would not agree, saying, "That would show weakness."
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor urgently asked to halt the project; Xueyan refused, saying, "That would show weakness.

sentences.zh: 即日巡塞上，撫定王兀堂諸部，聽於所在貿易。

translations.literal: That very day he toured the frontier, pacified Wang Wutang and the tribes, and allowed trade where they stood.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he toured the frontier, pacified Wang Wutang and the tribes, and allowed trade where they were.

sentences.zh: 卒築寬佃，斥地二百餘里。

translations.literal: He finally built Kuandian and opened more than two hundred li of land.
translations.idiomatic: He finally built Kuandian and opened more than two hundred li of land.

sentences.zh: 於是撫順以北，清河以南，皆遵約束。

translations.literal: Thereupon north of Fushun and south of Qinghe all kept to their agreements.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon from north of Fushun to south of Qinghe all kept their agreements.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，發兵誅王杲，大破之，追奔至紅力寨。

translations.literal: The next winter he sent troops to execute Wang Gao, inflicted a great defeat, and pursued the rout to Hongli Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he sent troops to execute Wang Gao, inflicted a great defeat, and pursued the rout to Hongli Stockade.

sentences.zh: 張居正第學顏功在總督楊兆上，加兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng ranked Xueyan's merit above supreme commander Yang Zhao's and promoted him to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng ranked Xueyan's merit above supreme commander Yang Zhao's and promoted him to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，土蠻大集諸部犯錦州，要求封王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, summer, the Tumen chieftain massed the tribes and attacked Jinzhou, demanding investiture as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year, the Tumen leader assembled the tribes, attacked Jinzhou, and demanded to be enfeoffed as a king.

sentences.zh: 學顏奏曰：「敵方憑陵，而與之通，是畏之也。

translations.literal: Xueyan memorialized, saying: "The enemy now presses upon us, yet to communicate with them is to show fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xueyan memorialized: "The enemy is bearing down on us; to negotiate with them would be to show fear.

sentences.zh: 制和者在彼，其和必不可久。

translations.literal: Those who control peace lie with them; such peace cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: The terms of peace would be dictated by them, and any truce could not endure.

sentences.zh: 且無功與有功同封，犯順與效順同賞，既取輕諸部，亦見笑俺答。

translations.literal: Moreover, to enfeoff the meritless together with the meritorious, and to reward the rebellious together with the obedient, would both slight the various tribes and make one a laughingstock to Altan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, granting the same honors to the undeserving and the deserving, and the same rewards to rebels and loyalists alike, would belittle the other tribes and invite Altan's ridicule.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹以正言卻之。」

translations.literal: Your ministers respectfully use upright words to refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers therefore respectfully decline in plain terms.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，敵亦引退。

translations.literal: Just then heavy rain fell, and the enemy also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment heavy rain fell, and the enemy withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 其冬，召為戎政侍郎，加右都御史。

translations.literal: That winter he was summoned as Vice Minister of Military Affairs and promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of Military Affairs and was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未受代，而土蠻約泰寧速把亥分犯遼、瀋、開原。

translations.literal: Before he could take over the post, the Tumen agreed with the Taining chieftain Subahai to divide forces and attack Liao, Shen, and Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the new office, the Tumen arranged with the Taining leader Subahai to raid Liao, Shen, and Kaiyuan in concert.

sentences.zh: 明年正月破敵劈山，殺其長阿醜臺等五人，學顏遂還部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he defeated the enemy at Pishan, killing their leader Achutai and four others; Xueyan then returned to his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he routed the enemy at Pishan, killing the chief Achutai and four others, after which Xueyan returned to the capital ministry.

sentences.zh: 逾年，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The year after, he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時張居正當國，以學顏精心計，深倚任之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Juzheng held power and, because Xueyan was skilled in accounts, deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng was then in charge of the government and, finding Xueyan meticulous in fiscal matters, placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 學顏撰會計錄以勾稽出納。

translations.literal: Xueyan compiled accounting records to audit receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan drew up accounting registers to track income and expenditure.

sentences.zh: 又奏列清丈條例，厘兩京、山東、陜西勛戚莊田，清溢額、脫漏、詭借諸弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized regulations for a comprehensive land survey, rectifying the estates of ennobled clans in the two capitals, Shandong, and Shaanxi, and clearing abuses of surplus quotas, omissions, and fraudulent transfers.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted rules for a nationwide land survey, regularized noble estates in the two capitals, Shandong, and Shaanxi, and remedied abuses involving excess holdings, concealed parcels, and false transfers.

sentences.zh: 又通行天下，得官民屯牧湖陂八十余萬頃。

translations.literal: He extended this throughout the empire and recovered more than eight hundred thousand mu of official, private, garrison, pasture, and lake land.
translations.idiomatic: The policy was applied empire-wide, recovering more than eight hundred thousand mu of official, private, garrison, pasture, and lake lands.

sentences.zh: 民困賠累者，以其賦抵之。

translations.literal: Those commoners burdened by compensation payments were allowed to offset them with their tax obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners crushed by compensation levies were permitted to offset them against their tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 自正、嘉虛耗之後，至萬歷十年間，最稱富庶，學顏有力焉。

translations.literal: From the wasteful years of the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns down to the tenth year of Wanli, the realm was at its most prosperous, and Xueyan had a strong hand in this.
translations.idiomatic: From the fiscal exhaustion of the Zhengde and Jiajing periods until the tenth year of Wanli, the empire enjoyed its greatest prosperity, to which Xueyan contributed substantially.

sentences.zh: 然是時宮闈用度汰侈，多所征索。

translations.literal: Yet at that time palace expenditures were extravagant and many levies were imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet palace spending had grown lavish and the court demanded ever more supplies.

sentences.zh: 學顏隨事納諫，得停發太倉銀十萬兩，減雲南黃金課一千兩，余多弗能執爭。

translations.literal: Xueyan remonstrated as each matter arose, securing suspension of one hundred thousand taels of silver from the Grand Granary and a reduction of one thousand taels in Yunnan's gold levy, but on much else he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan admonished the throne case by case, winning suspension of one hundred thousand taels from the Grand Granary and a cut of one thousand taels in Yunnan's gold levy, though on many other demands he could not hold the line.

sentences.zh: 而金花銀歲增二十萬兩，遂為定額。

translations.literal: The annual "flower silver" levy was increased by two hundred thousand taels and thereafter became a fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The annual "flower silver" levy rose by two hundred thousand taels and was thereafter fixed as a permanent quota.

sentences.zh: 人亦以是少之。

translations.literal: People therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: For this people thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 十一年四月，改兵部尚書，時方興內操，選內豎二千人雜廝養訓練，發太仆寺馬三千給之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year he was transferred to Minister of War; at that time inner-court drill was being promoted, two thousand eunuchs were chosen and mixed with menials for training, and three thousand horses from the Imperial Stud were issued to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eleventh year he was moved to Minister of War just as the palace was promoting inner-court drill: two thousand eunuchs were selected, trained together with servants, and three thousand horses from the Imperial Stud were assigned to them.

sentences.zh: 學顏執不與馬，又請停內操，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Xueyan refused to supply the horses and again asked that the inner drill be halted; neither request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan refused to release the horses and again asked that the inner drill be stopped; both pleas were ignored.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，車駕自山陵還，學顏上疏曰：「皇上恭奉聖母，扶輦前驅，拜祀陵園，考卜壽域，六軍將士十余萬，部伍齊肅。

translations.literal: That autumn, as the imperial carriage returned from the imperial tombs, Xueyan submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty respectfully attended the Empress Dowager, escorting her carriage ahead, worshipped at the tombs, and surveyed the burial ground; more than one hundred thousand soldiers of the six armies marched in disciplined ranks.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the emperor returned from the tombs, Xueyan memorialized: "Your Majesty dutifully escorted the Empress Dowager, led the procession to the tombs, and inspected the burial site, while more than one hundred thousand troops of the six armies kept perfect order.

sentences.zh: 惟內操隨駕軍士，進止自恣。

translations.literal: Only the inner-drill troops accompanying the carriage advanced and halted at will.
translations.idiomatic: Only the inner-drill soldiers following the carriage moved and halted as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 前至涼水河，喧爭無紀律，奔逸沖突，上動天顏。

translations.literal: Earlier, when they reached Liangshui River, they quarreled without discipline, broke ranks in collision, and disturbed the imperial countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Liangshui River, they brawled without discipline, broke ranks in a stampede, and provoked the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 今車駕已還，猶未解散。

translations.literal: Now that the carriage has returned, they have still not been dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the tour is over, they have still not been disbanded.

sentences.zh: 謹稽舊制，營軍隨駕郊祀，始受甲於內庫，事畢即還。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the old regulations: camp troops who accompanied the emperor on suburban sacrifices received armor from the inner storehouse only at the start and returned it when the rite ended.
translations.idiomatic: According to former practice, camp troops who escorted the emperor to suburban sacrifices received armor from the inner arsenal only for the occasion and returned it when the rite ended.

sentences.zh: 宮中惟長隨內侍許佩弓矢。

translations.literal: Within the palace only senior inner attendants were permitted to carry bow and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace only senior inner attendants were allowed to bear bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 又律：不系宿衛軍士，持寸刃入宮殿門者，絞；

translations.literal: The law also states: any soldier not on night guard who carries a blade of any length through a palace gate is strangled;
translations.idiomatic: The law further provides: any soldier not on night guard who carries even a short blade through a palace gate is strangled;

sentences.zh: 入皇城門者，戍邊衛。

translations.literal: one who enters a gate of the Imperial City is banished to a frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who enters a gate of the Imperial City is banished to a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 祖宗防微弭亂之意甚深且遠。

translations.literal: The intent of the founding emperors in guarding against the slightest disorder was very deep and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperors' intent in forestalling the slightest disorder was profound and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 今皇城內被甲乘馬持鋒刃，科道不得糾巡，臣部不得檢閱。

translations.literal: Now within the Imperial City men in armor ride horses bearing edged weapons, whom the censors cannot inspect on patrol and my ministry cannot review.
translations.idiomatic: Today, within the Imperial City, armored men ride horses with edged weapons—whom the censors cannot patrol and my ministry cannot inspect.

sentences.zh: 又招集廝養仆隸，出入禁苑，萬一驟起邪心，朋謀倡亂，嘩於內則外臣不敢入，嘩於夜則外兵不及知，嘩於都城白晝則曰天子親兵也，驅之不肯散，捕之莫敢攖。

translations.literal: Servants and menials are also gathered to enter the forbidden park; should they suddenly harbor evil intent and plot rebellion, if they riot within, outer officials dare not enter; if they riot at night, outer troops will not know in time; if they riot in broad daylight in the capital they will say they are the Son of Heaven's own troops—driven, they will not disperse; seized, none will dare resist.
translations.idiomatic: Servants and retainers are also admitted to the forbidden park. Should they suddenly turn traitorous and plot revolt, a riot inside would keep outer officials out; a riot at night would outpace the outer garrison; a riot by day in the capital would be called the emperor's own army—ordered to disperse, they would refuse; seized, none would dare resist.

sentences.zh: 正德中，西城練兵之事，良可鑒也。」

translations.literal: The affair of drilling troops in the western city during the Zhengde reign is a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: The western-city drill under the Zhengde emperor is a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 疏上，宦豎皆切齒，為蜚語中傷。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the eunuchs all gnashed their teeth and spread slander to injure him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the eunuchs seethed and spread slander against him.

sentences.zh: 神宗察知之，詰責主使者。

translations.literal: The Shenzong emperor perceived this and rebuked those who had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong saw through it and rebuked the instigators.

sentences.zh: 學顏得免，然亦不能用也。

translations.literal: Xueyan was spared, yet his proposals still could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan was spared, but his proposals were still not adopted.

sentences.zh: 考滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When his term of office was completed, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雲南嶽鳳、罕虔平，進太子太保。

translations.literal: When Yue Feng and Han Qian in Yunnan were pacified, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Yue Feng and Han Qian in Yunnan, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時張居正既歿，朝論大異。

translations.literal: By then Zhang Juzheng had died and court opinion greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhang Juzheng had died and opinion at court had shifted sharply.

sentences.zh: 初，御史劉臺以劾居正得罪，學顏復論其贓私。

translations.literal: Earlier, the censor Liu Tai had been punished for impeaching Juzheng; Xueyan again argued that Juzheng had been corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the censor Liu Tai had been punished for impeaching Juzheng; Xueyan now revived charges of Juzheng's corruption.

sentences.zh: 御史馮景隆論李成梁飾功，學顏亟稱成梁十大捷非妄，景隆坐貶斥。

translations.literal: The censor Feng Jinglong criticized Li Chengliang for embellishing his achievements; Xueyan repeatedly declared that Chengliang's ten great victories were no falsehood, and Jinglong was demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor Feng Jinglong accused Li Chengliang of inflating his merits, Xueyan insisted that Chengliang's ten great victories were genuine, and Jinglong was demoted and driven out.

sentences.zh: 學顏故為居正所厚，與李成梁共事久，物論皆以學顏黨於居正、成梁。

translations.literal: Xueyan had long been favored by Juzheng and had worked with Chengliang for many years; public opinion held that Xueyan sided with Juzheng and Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan had long been favored by Juzheng and had served with Chengliang for years; the public regarded him as Juzheng's and Chengliang's partisan.

sentences.zh: 御史孫繼先、曾乾亨、給事中黃道瞻交章論學顏。

translations.literal: The censors Sun Jixian and Zeng Qianheng and the supervising secretary Huang Daozhan submitted memorials in succession attacking Xueyan.
translations.idiomatic: The censors Sun Jixian and Zeng Qianheng and the supervising secretary Huang Daozhan memorialized against him in turn.

sentences.zh: 學顏疏辯求去，又請留道瞻，不聽。

translations.literal: Xueyan memorialized in defense and asked to leave office, and also asked that Daozhan be retained; neither request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan defended himself and asked to resign, and also asked that Daozhan be kept at his post; both requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 明年，順天府通判周弘禴又論學顏交通太監張鯨，神宗皆黜之於外。

translations.literal: The next year the Tongzhou assistant prefect Zhou Hongfu again accused Xueyan of dealings with the eunuch Zhang Jing; the Shenzong emperor dismissed them all from office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Tongzhou assistant prefect Zhou Hongfu again accused Xueyan of collusion with the eunuch Zhang Jing; Emperor Shenzong dismissed all the accusers from office.

sentences.zh: 學顏八疏乞休，許致仕去。

translations.literal: Xueyan submitted eight memorials begging to retire and was permitted to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyan submitted eight memorials begging retirement and was allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 二十六年；

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 張佳胤，字肖甫，銅梁人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiayin, style Xiaofu, was a native of Tongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiayin, courtesy name Xiaofu, was a native of Tongliang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 知滑縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Hua County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Hua County.

sentences.zh: 劇盜高章者，詐為緹騎，直入官署，劫佳胤索帑金。

translations.literal: The notorious bandit Gao Zhang pretended to be an imperial messenger, entered the yamen directly, and seized Jiayin to demand treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: A notorious bandit, Gao Zhang, posed as an imperial messenger, entered the magistrate's office, and seized Jiayin to extort government funds.

sentences.zh: 佳胤色不變，偽書券貸金，悉署遊僥名，召入立擒賊，由此知名。

translations.literal: Jiayin's expression did not change; he falsely wrote a note pledging borrowed gold, all signed with wandering idlers' names, summoned them in, and at once captured the bandits—thereby becoming famous.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin showed no fear; he forged a note promising borrowed gold, signed with the names of idle wanderers, summoned them inside, and seized the robbers at once—winning renown thereby.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部主事，改職方，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, transferred to the Bureau of Operations, and advanced to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, moved to the Bureau of Operations, and rose to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以風霾考察，謫陳州同知。

translations.literal: In the wind-and-dust evaluation he was demoted to vice prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In a review prompted by ominous winds he was demoted to vice prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷遷按察使。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年冬，擢右僉都御史，巡撫應天十府。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Longqing he was raised to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of the ten prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Longqing he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Yingtian's ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安慶兵變，坐勘獄辭不合，調南京鴻臚卿，就遷光祿。

translations.literal: When soldiers mutinied in Anqing, he was faulted because the language of his prison investigation did not conform and was transferred to Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing, then soon made Director of the Imperial Stables.
translations.idiomatic: After a mutiny in Anqing, he was transferred to Director of Ceremonies at Nanjing because his report on the prison case was deemed improper, and was soon made Director of the Imperial Stables.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，巡撫保定，道聞喪歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding; on the road he heard of a bereavement and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding, but on the way learned of a death in the family and returned home.

sentences.zh: 萬歷七年，起故官，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli he was recalled to his former post and made grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wanli he was recalled to his former rank and appointed grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上，改宣府。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed office he was transferred to Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 時青把都已服，其弟滿五大猶桀驁，所部八賴掠塞外史、車二部，總兵官麻錦擒之。

translations.literal: At that time the Qingbatu tribe had submitted, but his younger brother Mandawu remained defiant; his follower Balai raided the Saiwai Shi and Che tribes beyond the border, and the regional commander Ma Jin captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingbatu Mongols had already submitted, but Mandawu, younger brother of the chieftain, remained defiant; his follower Balai raided the Shi and Che tribes beyond the border, and the regional commander Ma Jin captured him.

sentences.zh: 佳胤命錦縛八賴將斬，而身馳赦之，八賴叩頭誓不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: Jiayin ordered Jin to bind Balai for execution, then himself galloped ahead to pardon him; Balai kowtowed and swore never again to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin ordered Jin to bind Balai for execution, then rode ahead himself to grant a pardon; Balai kowtowed and swore never again to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後與總督鄭洛計服滿五大。

translations.literal: Later, together with the governor-general Zheng Luo, he planned to bring Mandawu to submission.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Governor-General Zheng Luo, he devised means to bring Mandawu to submission.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十年春，浙江巡撫吳善言奉詔減月餉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year the Zhejiang grand coordinator Wu Shanyan, obeying an edict, reduced monthly pay.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year the Zhejiang grand coordinator Wu Shanyan, carrying out an edict, cut the troops' monthly pay.

sentences.zh: 東、西二營兵馬文英、劉廷用等構黨大噪，縛毆善言。

translations.literal: Ma Wenying and Liu Tingyong of the eastern and western camps formed factions and raised a great clamor, binding and beating Shanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wenying and Liu Tingyong of the eastern and western camps formed factions, raised a great uproar, and bound and beat Shanyan.

sentences.zh: 張居正以佳胤才，令兼右僉都御史代善言。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng, because of Jiayin's ability, ordered him to take on concurrently the post of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in Shanyan's place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, valuing Jiayin's ability, had him concurrently appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace Shanyan.

sentences.zh: 甫入境，而杭民以行保甲故，亦亂。

translations.literal: As soon as he entered the territory, the Hangzhou populace also rioted because of the implementation of the baojia system.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he entered the province when the people of Hangzhou also rioted over the baojia household-registration system.

sentences.zh: 佳胤問告者曰：「亂兵與亂民合乎？」

translations.literal: Jiayin asked the informant: "Have the mutinous soldiers joined with the mutinous people?
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin asked his informants: "Have the mutinous soldiers and the rioting populace joined forces?

sentences.zh: 曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 佳胤喜曰：「速驅之，尚可離而二也。」

translations.literal: Jiayin said with pleasure: "Drive them off quickly—they can still be separated into two."
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin said gladly: "Drive them apart quickly—they can still be kept separate."

sentences.zh: 既至，民剽益甚。

translations.literal: After he arrived, the people's pillaging grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: After his arrival the people's looting grew worse.

sentences.zh: 佳胤從數卒佯問民所苦，下令除之。

translations.literal: Jiayin went with a few attendants, pretending to ask what the people suffered from, and issued orders abolishing the grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin went out with only a few attendants, feigning inquiry into the people's hardships, and issued orders removing their grievances.

sentences.zh: 眾益張，夜掠巨室，火光燭天。

translations.literal: The crowd grew bolder; by night they plundered great houses and firelight lit the sky.
translations.idiomatic: The mob grew bolder; by night they looted great houses until firelight filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 佳胤召遊擊徐景星諭二營兵，令討亂民自贖。

translations.literal: Jiayin summoned the mobile-detachment commander Xu Jingxing and instructed the troops of the two camps to suppress the rioting populace to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayin summoned the mobile-detachment commander Xu Jingxing and ordered the two camps' soldiers to suppress the rioters as penance.

sentences.zh: 擒百五十人，斬其三之一。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty were captured and one third of them were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty were seized and a third of them were executed.

sentences.zh: 乃佯召文英、廷用，予冠帶。

translations.literal: He then pretended to summon Wenying and Tingyong and gave them caps and belts.
translations.idiomatic: He then feigned a summons to Wenying and Tingyong and bestowed caps and belts on them.

sentences.zh: 而密屬景星捕七人，並文英、廷用斬之。

translations.literal: Secretly he ordered Jingxing to arrest seven men and beheaded them together with Wenying and Tingyong.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he told Jingxing to arrest seven men and beheaded them together with Wenying and Tingyong.

sentences.zh: 二亂悉定。

translations.literal: Both disturbances were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Both disturbances were quelled.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒美。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict of praise and commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict praising his service.

sentences.zh: 尋以左侍郎還部，錄功，加右都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to the ministry as Left Vice Minister and, when merits were recorded, was given the additional title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to the ministry as Left Vice Minister; when merits were recorded he received the additional title Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜戎政尚書，尋兼右副都御史，總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Military Affairs and soon also Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, governing military affairs in Ji, Liao, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Minister of Military Affairs and soon also Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, with overall command of Ji, Liao, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以李成梁擊斬逞加努功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Because Li Chengliang's achievement in attacking and killing Chengjianu was recognized, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chengliang's feat in killing Chengjianu was recognized, Jiayin was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 成梁破土蠻沈陽，復進太子太保。

translations.literal: When Chengliang broke the Tumen at Shenyang, he was further promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengliang routed the Tumen at Shenyang, he was further promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 召還理部事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to manage the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to manage the ministry.

sentences.zh: 敘勞，予一品誥。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed he was granted a patent of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were distributed he received a patent of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 御史許守恩劾佳胤營獲本兵，御史徐元復劾之，遂三疏謝病歸。

translations.literal: The censor Xu Shouen impeached Jiayin for seizing the post of Minister of War; the censor Xu Yuan again impeached him, and he submitted three memorials begging leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Xu Shouen impeached Jiayin for usurping the Ministry of War; the censor Xu Yuan impeached him again, and he submitted three memorials pleading illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 越二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚襄憲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was given the posthumous title Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianqi reign he was given the posthumous title Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 殷正茂，字養實，歙人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhengmao, style Yangshi, was a native of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhengmao, courtesy name Yangshi, was a native of She County.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 由行人選兵科給事中。

translations.literal: From the post of courier he was selected as supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War.
translations.idiomatic: From the post of courier he was chosen supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War.

sentences.zh: 劾罷南京刑部侍郎沈應龍。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed the Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing, Shen Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed Shen Yinglong, Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 歷廣西、雲南、湖廣兵備副使，遷江西按察使。

translations.literal: He served as vice commissioner for military preparedness in Guangxi, Yunnan, and Huguang, and was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner for military preparedness in Guangxi, Yunnan, and Huguang, then was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，古田僮韋銀豹、黃朝猛反。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing the Yao Wei Yinbao and Huang Chaomeng of Gutian rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing the Gutian Yao chiefs Wei Yinbao and Huang Chaomeng rebelled.

sentences.zh: 銀豹父朝威自弘治中敗官兵於三厄，殺副總兵馬俊、參議馬鉉，正德中嘗陷洛容。

translations.literal: Yinbao's father Chaowei, from the Hongzhi period onward, had defeated government troops at San'e, killed Vice Commander-in-Chief Ma Jun and Assistant Commissioner Ma Xuan, and in the Zhengde period had once taken Luorong.
translations.idiomatic: Yinbao's father Chaowei, since the Hongzhi era, had defeated government forces at San'e, killed Vice Commander Ma Jun and Assistant Commissioner Ma Xuan, and in the Zhengde reign had once seized Luorong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，銀豹及朝猛劫殺參政黎民衷，提督侍郎吳桂芳遣典史廖元招降之。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period Yinbao and Chaomeng murdered and plundered, killing Assistant Commissioner Li Min'ai; the supervising vice minister Wu Guifang sent the clerk Liao Yuan to summon them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing period Yinbao and Chaomeng murdered and plundered, killing Assistant Commissioner Li Min'ai; Supervising Vice Minister Wu Guifang sent the clerk Liao Yuan to offer surrender terms.

sentences.zh: 遷元主簿以守，而銀豹數反覆。

translations.literal: Yuan was promoted to registrar to guard the area, yet Yinbao repeatedly wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was promoted to registrar to hold the district, but Yinbao vacillated again and again.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年冬，廷議大征。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Longqing the court resolved on a major campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Longqing the court decided on a major expedition.

sentences.zh: 擢正茂右僉都御史巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: Zhengmao was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengmao was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 正茂與提督李遷調土、漢兵十四萬，令總兵俞大猷將之。

translations.literal: Zhengmao, together with the supervising general Li Qian, mustered one hundred forty thousand native and Han troops and ordered the regional commander Yu Dayou to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: With Supervising General Li Qian he assembled one hundred forty thousand native and Han troops and placed Regional Commander Yu Dayou in command.

sentences.zh: 先奪牛河、三厄險，諸軍連克東山鳳凰寨，蹙之潮水。

translations.literal: They first seized the strongholds of Niuhe and San'e; the armies in succession took the Dongshan Fenghuang stockade and drove the enemy to the Chaoshui narrows.
translations.idiomatic: They first took the strongholds at Niuhe and San'e; the armies in succession captured the Dongshan Fenghuang stockade and pressed the enemy to the Chaoshui narrows.

sentences.zh: 廖元誘僮人斬朝猛，銀豹窮，令其黨陰斬貌類己者以獻。

translations.literal: Liao Yuan induced the Yao to behead Chaomeng; Yinbao, cornered, had his followers secretly kill a man resembling himself to present the head.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yuan induced the Yao to behead Chaomeng; cornered, Yinbao had his men secretly kill someone resembling himself and present the head.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進兵部右侍郎，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War while remaining grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported he was promoted to Vice Minister of War while retaining the grand coordinator post.

sentences.zh: 改古田為永寧州，設副使參將鎮守。

translations.literal: Gutian was changed to Yongning Prefecture and a vice commissioner and regional commander were stationed to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Gutian was redesignated Yongning Prefecture, with a vice commissioner and regional commander stationed there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，僉事金柱捕得銀豹，正茂因自劾。

translations.literal: Before long the registrar Jin Zhu captured Yinbao; Zhengmao thereupon submitted a self-impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Registrar Jin Zhu captured Yinbao; Zhengmao then impeached himself.

sentences.zh: 詔磔銀豹京師，置正茂不問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yinbao dismembered at the capital and Zhengmao left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yinbao executed by dismemberment in the capital and excused Zhengmao.

sentences.zh: 尋代遷提督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Qian as supervising general of the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Li Qian as supervising general of the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 當是時，群盜惠州藍一清、賴元爵，潮州林道乾、林鳳、諸良寶，瓊州李茂，處處屯結。

translations.literal: At that time bandits Lan Yiqing and Lai Yuanjue of Huizhou, Lin Daoqian, Lin Feng, and Zhu Liangbao of Chaozhou, and Li Mao of Qiongzhou were entrenched everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were entrenched everywhere: Lan Yiqing and Lai Yuanjue in Huizhou, Lin Daoqian, Lin Feng, and Zhu Liangbao in Chaozhou, and Li Mao in Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣中日告警，倭又數為害。

translations.literal: Guangdong daily sounded alarms, and the Japanese pirates also repeatedly did harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was in daily alarm, and Japanese raiders struck again and again.

sentences.zh: 正茂議守巡官畫地分守，而徙瀕海謫戍之民於雲南、川、湖，絕倭向導。

translations.literal: Zhengmao proposed that defending and touring officials divide the territory for defense, and that exiled coastal people be moved to Yunnan, Sichuan, and Huguang to cut off Japanese guides.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengmao proposed that defending and touring officials divide the territory for defense, and that exiles on the coast be resettled in Yunnan, Sichuan, and Huguang to deny the Japanese local guides.

sentences.zh: 乃令總兵官張元勛、參政江一麟等先後殺倭千余，以次盡平諸盜。

translations.literal: He then ordered the regional commander Zhang Yuanxun, the assistant commissioner Jiang Yilin, and others in succession to kill more than a thousand Japanese and thereafter pacify the bandits one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Regional Commander Zhang Yuanxun, Assistant Commissioner Jiang Yilin, and others kill more than a thousand Japanese in turn and thereafter pacify the bandits one by one.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫郭應聘亦奏平懷遠、洛容瑤，語詳元勛及李錫傳。

translations.literal: The Guangxi grand coordinator Guo Yingpin also reported pacifying the Huaiyuan and Luorong Yao; the details are given in the biographies of Yuanxun and Li Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi grand coordinator Guo Yingpin also reported pacifying the Huaiyuan and Luorong Yao; particulars appear in the biographies of Zhang Yuanxun and Li Xi.

sentences.zh: 正茂以功累加兵部尚書兼右副都御史。

translations.literal: Zhengmao, for his achievements, was repeatedly promoted to Minister of War with the additional title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements Zhengmao was repeatedly promoted until he held the posts of Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 倭復陷銅鼓、雙魚，元勛大破之儒峒；

translations.literal: The Japanese again took Tonggu and Shuangyu; Yuanxun heavily defeated them at Rudong;
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese again seized Tonggu and Shuangyu; Yuanxun routed them heavily at Rudong;

sentences.zh: 犯電白，正茂剿殺千余人。

translations.literal: they invaded Dianbai and Zhengmao hunted down and killed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: when they invaded Dianbai, Zhengmao pursued and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 嶺表略定。

translations.literal: Lingnan was largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan was largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三年，召為南京戶部尚書，以淩雲翼代。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli he was summoned as Minister of Revenue at Nanjing; Ling Yunyi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wanli he was summoned to be Minister of Revenue at Nanjing; Ling Yunyi replaced him.

sentences.zh: 明年，改北部。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the northern ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the northern ministry.

sentences.zh: 疏請節用，又諫止采買珠寶。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking for economy and again remonstrated against purchasing pearls and gems.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized urging frugality and again remonstrated against procuring pearls and gems.

sentences.zh: 而張居正以正茂所饋鵝罽轉奉慈寧太后為坐褥。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng, because of the goose-down rug Zhengmao had presented, had it turned over to the Empress Dowager Cining as a seat cushion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng took the goose-down rug Zhengmao had presented and had it sent to Empress Dowager Cining as a seat cushion.

sentences.zh: 李幼孜與爭寵，嗾言官詹沂等劾之。

translations.literal: Li Youzi, contending for favor, incited the censor Zhan Yi and others to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youzi, competing for influence, incited the censor Zhan Yi and others to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 遂屢引疾。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 六年，致仕歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 久之，起南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was again appointed Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again appointed Minister of Justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 居正卒之明年，御史張應詔言，正茂以金盤二，植珊瑚其中，高三尺許，賂居正，復取金珠、翡翠、象牙饋馮保及居正家人遊七。

translations.literal: In the year after Juzheng's death the censor Zhang Yingzhao said that Zhengmao had given Juzheng two gold trays with coral planted in them more than three feet high, and again presented gold, pearls, jadeite, and ivory to the eunuch Feng Bao and to Juzheng's household retainer You Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after Juzheng's death the censor Zhang Yingzhao charged that Zhengmao had given Juzheng two gold trays with coral set in them standing more than three feet high, and had also sent gold, pearls, jadeite, and ivory to the eunuch Feng Bao and to Juzheng's retainer You Qi.

sentences.zh: 正茂疏辨，請告，許之。

translations.literal: Zhengmao memorialized in defense and asked leave; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengmao defended himself in a memorial and asked to retire; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he died.

sentences.zh: 正茂在廣時，任法嚴，道將以下奉行惟謹。

translations.literal: While Zhengmao was in Guangdong his enforcement of law was strict and commanders and defenders below him obeyed with trepidation.
translations.idiomatic: While in Guangdong Zhengmao enforced the law strictly; commanders and defenders obeyed him in fear.

sentences.zh: 然性貪，歲受屬吏金萬計。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was greedy; each year he received tens of thousands in gold from subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was greedy by nature and each year accepted tens of thousands in gold from subordinates.

sentences.zh: 初征古田，大學士高拱曰：「吾捐百萬金予正茂，縱幹沒者半，然事可立辦。」

translations.literal: When the campaign against Gutian began, the Grand Secretary Gao Gong said: "I will give Zhengmao a million in gold; even if he embezzles half, the affair can still be quickly concluded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gutian campaign began, Grand Secretary Gao Gong said: "I will give Zhengmao a million in gold; even if he pockets half, the business can still be finished quickly.

sentences.zh: 時以拱為善用人。

translations.literal: At the time people regarded Gong as skilled in employing men.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time regarded Gao Gong as skilled at using men.

sentences.zh: 李遷，字子安，新建人。

translations.literal: Li Qian, style Zi'an, was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian, courtesy name Zi'an, was a native of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年官南京兵部右侍郎，以左侍郎總督兩廣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he held the post of Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing and, as Left Vice Minister, supervised the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Longqing he was Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing and, as Left Vice Minister, supervised military affairs in the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 給事中光懋言兩廣向設提督，事權畫一，今兩巡撫相牽掣，不便。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Guang Mao said that the two Guang had formerly had a single supervising general with unified authority, but now the two grand coordinators checked each other, which was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Guang Mao argued that the two provinces had once had a single supervising general with unified authority, whereas two grand coordinators now hindered each other.

sentences.zh: 乃改遷提督兼巡撫廣東，而特命正茂為廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: Qian was therefore made supervising general while also grand coordinator of Guangdong, and Zhengmao was specially appointed grand coordinator of Guangxi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was therefore made supervising general while also grand coordinator of Guangdong, and Zhengmao was specially appointed grand coordinator of Guangxi alone.

sentences.zh: 後遂為定制。

translations.literal: This later became the fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This later became the permanent arrangement.

sentences.zh: 以平銀豹功加右都御史。

translations.literal: For pacifying Yinbao he was given the additional title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Yinbao he received the additional title Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋討惠、潮山寇，俘斬千二百余級。

translations.literal: Soon he campaigned against the mountain bandits of Hui and Chao and captured or beheaded more than twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he campaigned against the mountain bandits of Huizhou and Chaozhou, capturing or beheading more than twelve hundred.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 謚恭介。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gongjie.

sentences.zh: 遷出入中外三十年，不妄取一錢。

translations.literal: Qian served inside and outside the government for thirty years and never took a single cash unrightfully.
translations.idiomatic: Qian served inside and outside the government for thirty years without ever taking a single cash unrightfully.

sentences.zh: 年近七十，母終，廬墓。

translations.literal: When he was nearly seventy his mother died and he built a hut at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nearly seventy his mother died and he lived in a mourning hut at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 淩雲翼，字洋山，太倉州人。

translations.literal: Ling Yunyi, style Yangshan, was a native of Taicang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Yunyi, courtesy name Yangshan, was a native of Taicang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，累官右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period he rose step by step to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and pacification commissioner of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Longqing he rose step by step to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and pacification commissioner of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 疏論衛所兵消耗之弊，凡六事，多議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized on six points regarding the wasting away of garrison troops; most were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on six abuses eroding garrison forces; most of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，進右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wanli he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 三遷兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史，提督兩廣軍務，代殷正茂。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Left Vice Minister of War with the additional title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supervising military affairs in the two Guang provinces in place of Yin Zhengmao.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Left Vice Minister of War with the additional title Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supervising the two Guang in Yin Zhengmao's place.

sentences.zh: 時寇盜略盡，惟林鳳遁去。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were largely gone; only Lin Feng had fled.
translations.idiomatic: By then bandits were largely gone; only Lin Feng remained at large.

sentences.zh: 鳳初屯錢澳求撫，正茂不許，遂自彭湖奔東番魍港，為福建總兵官胡守仁所敗。

translations.literal: Feng had first encamped at Qian'ao seeking surrender; Zhengmao did not permit it, so he fled from Penghu to Wugang in eastern Taiwan and was defeated by the Fujian regional commander Hu Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had first camped at Qian'ao seeking surrender; Zhengmao refused, so he fled from Penghu to Wugang in eastern Taiwan and was defeated by Fujian's regional commander Hu Shouren.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，犯柘林、靖海、碣石，已，復犯福建。

translations.literal: That winter he raided Zhelin, Jinghai, and Jieshi, and afterward again raided Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he raided Zhelin, Jinghai, and Jieshi, and later struck Fujian again.

sentences.zh: 守仁追擊至淡水洋，沈其舟二十。

translations.literal: Shouren pursued him to the Freshwater Sea and sank twenty of his boats.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren pursued him to the Freshwater Sea and sank twenty of his vessels.

sentences.zh: 賊失利，復入潮州。

translations.literal: The bandits suffered defeat and again entered Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, the pirates re-entered Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 參政金淛諭降其黨馬誌善、李成等，鳳夜遁。

translations.literal: The assistant commissioner Jin Zhe induced Ma Zhishan, Li Cheng, and others to surrender; Feng fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commissioner Jin Zhe induced Ma Zhishan, Li Cheng, and others to surrender; Feng fled by night.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，把總王望高以呂宋番兵討平之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the following year the company commander Wang Wangao, with Luzon auxiliaries, campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the next year Company Commander Wang Wangao, with Luzon auxiliaries, campaigned and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 尋進征羅旁。

translations.literal: Soon he undertook the campaign against Luopang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he launched the campaign against Luopang.

sentences.zh: 羅旁在德慶州上下江界、東西兩山間，延袤七百里。

translations.literal: Luopang lay between the upper and lower reaches of the river boundary in Deqing Prefecture and between the eastern and western mountains, extending seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Luopang lay between the upper and lower river boundaries of Deqing Prefecture and between the eastern and western mountains, stretching seven hundred li.

sentences.zh: 成化中，韓雍經略西山，頗安輯，惟東山瑤阻深箐剽掠，有司歲發卒戍守。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua period Han Yong had pacified the western hills and brought considerable order, but the eastern-hill Yao in deep ravines still plundered, and the authorities sent troops to garrison each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua period Han Yong had pacified the western hills, but eastern-hill Yao in deep ravines still raided, and the government sent garrisons every year.

sentences.zh: 正茂方建議大征，會遷去。

translations.literal: Zhengmao had just proposed a major campaign when Qian left office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengmao had just proposed a major campaign when Li Qian left office.

sentences.zh: 雲翼乃大集兵，令兩廣總兵張元勛、李錫將之。

translations.literal: Yunyi then massed troops and ordered the regional commanders of the two Guang, Zhang Yuanxun and Li Xi, to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi then massed troops and placed the two Guang regional commanders Zhang Yuanxun and Li Xi in command.

sentences.zh: 四閱月，克巢五百六十，俘斬、招降四萬二千八百余人。

translations.literal: In four months they took five hundred sixty lairs, capturing, beheading, or accepting the surrender of more than forty-two thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In four months they stormed five hundred sixty lairs, capturing, killing, or accepting the surrender of more than forty-two thousand eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 岑溪六十三山、七山、那留、連城諸處鄰境瑤、僮皆懼。

translations.literal: The neighboring Yao and Zhuang of the sixty-three mountains of Cenxi, the seven mountains, Naliu, and Liancheng all grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring Yao and Zhuang of Cenxi's sixty-three mountains, the seven mountains, Naliu, and Liancheng all grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 賊首潘積善求撫，雲翼奏設官戍之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Pan Jishan sought surrender; Yunyi memorialized to establish officials and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chief Pan Jishan sought surrender; Yunyi memorialized to station officials and troops.

sentences.zh: 論功，加右都御史兼兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the additional title of Right Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he received the additional titles Right Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 賜飛魚服。

translations.literal: He was granted the flying-fish robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the flying-fish robe.

sentences.zh: 乃改瀧水縣為羅定州，設監司、參將。

translations.literal: Longshui County was then changed to Luoding Prefecture and surveillance commissioners and regional commanders were established.
translations.idiomatic: Longshui County was redesignated Luoding Prefecture, with surveillance commissioners and regional commanders installed.

sentences.zh: 積患頓息。

translations.literal: Long-standing troubles suddenly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic disorders abruptly ceased.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，與巡撫吳文華討平河池、咘咳、北三諸瑤，又捕斬廣東大廟諸山賊。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, together with the grand coordinator Wu Wenhua, he campaigned and pacified the Yao of Hechi, Buke, and the northern three districts, and again hunted down and beheaded the mountain bandits of Damiao in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year, with Grand Coordinator Wu Wenhua, he pacified the Yao of Hechi, Buke, and the northern three districts, and again hunted down the mountain bandits of Damiao in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嶺表悉定。

translations.literal: Lingnan was entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 召為南京工部尚書，就改兵部，以兵部尚書兼右副都御史總督漕運，巡撫淮、揚。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Works at Nanjing, then transferred to the Ministry of War, and as Minister of War with the additional title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he supervised the Grand Canal transport and was grand coordinator of Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Works at Nanjing, then moved to the Ministry of War, and as Minister of War with the additional title Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he supervised Grand Canal transport and served as grand coordinator of Huai and Yang.

sentences.zh: 河臣潘季馴召入，遂兼督河道。

translations.literal: When the river official Pan Jixun was recalled, Yunyi also took charge of the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: When river commissioner Pan Jixun was recalled, Yunyi also took charge of the waterways.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 召為戎政尚書，以病歸。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Military Affairs and returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Military Affairs and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 家居驕縱，給事、御史連章劾之。

translations.literal: At home he was arrogant and unrestrained; supervising secretaries and censors memorialized against him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At home he grew arrogant and unrestrained; supervising secretaries and censors memorialized against him in turn.

sentences.zh: 詔奪官，後卒。

translations.literal: An edict stripped him of office; he died later.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of rank; he died afterward.

sentences.zh: 雲翼有幹濟才。

translations.literal: Yunyi had talent for practical administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyi had talent for practical administration.

sentences.zh: 羅旁之役，繼正茂成功。

translations.literal: In the Luopang campaign he followed on Zhengmao's success.
translations.idiomatic: In the Luopang campaign he built on Zhengmao's success.

sentences.zh: 然喜事好殺戮，為當時所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in action and favored killing; he was ridiculed by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he delighted in action and favored killing, and contemporaries mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：譚綸、王崇古諸人，受任巖疆，練達兵備，可與余子俊、秦纮先後比跡。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tan Lun, Wang Chonggu, and the others, charged with the frontier marches, were practiced in military preparedness and may be compared in succession with Yu Zijun and Qin Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Tan Lun, Wang Chonggu, and their fellows, entrusted with the frontier marches, were skilled in military preparedness and may be ranked with Yu Zijun and Qin Hong.

sentences.zh: 考其時，蓋張居正當國，究心於軍謀邊瑣。

translations.literal: Examining their time, it was when Zhang Juzheng held the government and devoted his mind to military plans and border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Consider their era: Zhang Juzheng held power and devoted himself to military plans and border affairs.

sentences.zh: 書疏往復，洞矚機要，委任責成，使得展布，是以各盡其材，事克有濟。

translations.literal: Letters and memorials went back and forth; he penetrated the crucial points, entrusted responsibility, and demanded results, so that they could deploy their talents—thus each fulfilled his capacity and affairs succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials flowed back and forth; he grasped the crucial points, delegated responsibility, and demanded results, allowing each man to deploy his talents—so affairs were brought to success.

sentences.zh: 觀於此，而居正之功不可泯也。

translations.literal: Seen in this light, Juzheng's achievement cannot be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, Juzheng's achievement cannot be denied.
